c.form(class_form=).why: The keyword landed but every power printing it is above the imported tier, so there is no form anything can enter and no state to gate on. `todo=` rather than `dropped=` is right: there is no payout to withhold.

c.form(forbids=).why: c.form returns the Effect, durations runs on_end for every ending alike, and f1707b next door already hangs a teardown there

c.form(keeps_gear=).why: c.forbid takes a ref or a Keyword and cls=ITEM is neither, so item powers cannot be suspended as a class; only the shield half is writable

c.form(mimics=).why: c.in_form answers which shape, and the row correctly rules it out: what is needed is whether the shape is *that particular creature's*, which c.form cannot be told and nothing records. The naming half is already closed (p2472 is declared).

c.form(on_revert=).why: c.form returns the Effect and already appends to its on_end itself; over-fires only in that the clock ending the form also pays the shift

c.form(return_within=).why: c.form's way out is Effect.drop_cost and actions._dropping offers it with no predicate of any kind

c.gains_advantage(weapon=).why: resolve.attack builds its gate ctx as attacker/target/power plus kind for ranged and never a weapon

c.gains_property(against=).why: writes replace(w) copies into Gear.weapons and every reader takes no context, so a property cannot know who the blow is aimed at

c.gains_property(implement=).why: writes Weapon.properties and the implement attack path never reads them, so there is no second door for one object to answer two paths

c.gains_property(in_zone=).why: c.grants_in carries a numeric modifier, not a property, and c.gains_property writes onto a carried copy with no undo

c.grab(attackable=).why: A grab is a relation between two entities (Relation.GRABBED_BY, c.grab(by=)) and nothing makes a limb an attackable thing with its own defences. m3300a3 says it checked this against cast.py, and the cap it also needed already works without this row.

c.grab(bonus=).why: i1468x1 says 'c.grab simply takes hold -- there is no roll for a modifier to reach', but c.grab_attempt rolls Strength vs Reflex with as_='grab' and as_ rides the attack ctx; c.bull_rush's docstring records that 14 modifiers already gate on the same key.

c.grab(dc_from=).why: grab(dc=) stores an int for escape.attempt, and c.grab's docstring reserves this case under #421: a DC that is another creature's defence could never be satisfied by dc=int

c.grab(pull_as_minor=).why: c.grant_action reads only shift/stand/escape/second_wind and actions.legal builds no grabbed-move entry

c.grab(unbreakable=).why: c.grab has one behaviour; durability against forced movement has no parameter and no component field

c.grab(until=).why: c.grab hands back the Effect and c.end_effect's docstring says a row keeps its own hold in a local and ends it from a watch; Effects._lift clears the triple

c.grab_reach().why: Relation.GRABBED_BY means adjacent and nothing else, so a hold that reaches two squares has no expression. (m5648a3's docstring also claims c.grab takes no dc, which its own body contradicts with dc=13 -- a separate stale note.)

c.grabbing(auto_share=).why: m6113a0 is accurate: `share=True` already drags a grabbed creature along for one call, and nothing makes every future move do it without being told. The standing licence would be a movement-layer flag that does not exist, and the printed check has no grab check in this tree to modify.

c.grant_action('light').why: c.grant_action reads only four words, and the grant-a-row alternative needs a second ref; f2117b, the feat's only spare, is spent on the radiant rider

c.grant_action('mount').why: c.grant_action's docstring prescribes exactly this work: 'anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing, so add the reader in actions at the same time as the word'. actions.legal already does it for stand (reading _granted for the cheaper cost), and c.ride is the payload. A word plus a menu reader, not a mechanism.

c.grant_action('move_zone').why: c.give makes a real menu line with an arbitrary payout; unconfirmed because the carrier is a uses-counted Item, so a standing per-turn line needs the count refreshed

c.grant_action('teleport').why: actions._granted is consumed for shift/stand/escape/second_wind/instinctive/command only; any other word is stored and never read

c.grant_action(charge).found: c.grant_action (its own docstring: 'anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing, so add the reader in actions at the same time as the word'), actions._charges, c.charge_at
c.grant_action(charge).why: The charge exists twice over -- as an action menu entry and as a verb -- so the word only needs the reader the verb's docstring already prescribes. This is the thin door onto something that works, not a mechanism.

c.grant_action(conjuration_attack).why: grant_action's what is read for four words only, and c.recast re-runs the whole row rather than making the standing shape swing

c.grant_action(familiar=).why: The same documented extension point as c.grant_action('mount'): add the word and its reader in actions, which legal already does for stand. c.move_companion is the payload and works. One word and one menu branch.

c.grant_action(move).why: the vocabulary is four words and anything else is carried, costs nothing and does nothing; a free hop between two squares of a zone is none of them

c.grant_action(move_grabbed).why: the same gap from the other side; this and c.grab(pull_as_minor=) are one gap under two symbols

c.grant_action(standard).why: c.extra_action "drops one action into the budget the turn is already spending, which Encounter.can reads back", takes any ActionType and an on=, and announces ActionGranted - whose docstring calls Cast.extra_action "the one door". m4488a2's and m5460a4's "takes a standard action" is c.extra_action(ActionType.STANDARD); c.grant_action's closed four-word list was the wrong verb to look at.

c.grant_action(toward=).why: carries a cost and a count and nothing about where the granted step may end, and the shift is taken later by another creature

c.grant_action(trigger=).why: f3210 and f3204 both gate a granted shift on a trigger by laying c.grant_action from inside a watch, so the watch is the condition

c.grant_action(when=).why: the signature has no gate and the option is built in actions.legal rather than evaluated at arming

c.grant_armor().found: nothing (c.as_weapon is the analogue, with no mirror)
c.grant_armor().why: c.as_weapon exists for the weapon side of the same sentence and there is no armour equivalent - nothing puts a worn item on a creature mid-fight, so an enhancement bonus and the item's columns have nowhere to live. p16411 names c.grant_weapon() as the sibling marker group.

c.grant_attack(kind=).why: cast.py:1935 already lays Mod(what='attack', value=attack_bonus, kind='power'), so the row is getting the power bonus it says it cannot have. Its docstring is wrong

c.grant_attack(upgrade=).why: PowerUsed is a plain Event, not a Decision, so the swing already being handed over cannot be cancelled or swapped from this window

c.grant_inline().found: a coined ref plus c.grant_row -- the f1253/f1253b and rt:/cf: precedent
c.grant_inline().why: i1188p1 and i2980p1 both say the granted power 'has no ref of its own'. Content coins refs routinely for rows the compendium does not number (f1253b via _swap, every rt: and cf:), the author has the card's full text in the brief, and c.grant_row then hands the declared row over -- so these are rows to write rather than a facility to build.

c.grant_trait(mount).why: m3288a8 says 'nothing on the board records that one creature is riding another'. Relation.RIDDEN_BY does, and c.mount() returns the ridden creature -- m4027a4's docstring states it outright ('the mount half needs nothing new -- c.ride, c.mount and c.rider already exist'). The trait is c.ignores_difficult(on=c.mount()).

c.grant_weapon().why: i1261x1 says 'nothing adds one to Gear.weapons from a body'; as_weapon builds a Weapon and appends it to Gear.weapons, stowed so actions._wielding offers the draw. Armour-that-is-also-a-weapon is the same shape as the shield-as-weapon the verb was written for.

c.grants_advantage(everyone=).why: query.grants_ca derives only from conditions, every one of which carries other penalties, and _NEUTRAL only turns the flag off

c.grants_advantage(until_save=).why: durations fires on_end for a saving throw as well as a clock; unconfirmed is reaching that hold, since the feat answers Hit, announced before the save-ends effect is laid

c.grants_in(advantage=).why: takes a live when= gate, as cf:shaman-f0s2 lays a position-gated c.no_cover; iterating c.enemies() with a within-3 gate is the standing condition

c.grants_in(unless=).why: when= is on the signature and handed to c.bonus per beneficiary via _while_inside; skills builds the ctx with actor/skill/target. The row's 'no predicate' is false

c.guild_training().why: i998x1 adds to the temporary hit points a named class feature hands out, and nothing models that feature or announces its payout -- the same family as `c.class_feature()` and with the same root: the feature has no row.

c.half_damage(when=).why: c.halve(ev) takes an explicit event and DamageRolled.amount is writable; the pattern c.half_healing uses internally and p14189 uses in content

c.half_healing(amount=).why: a Window.BEFORE watcher doing ev.amount //= 2 with no flat form; the only flat docking anywhere is a surge value, not healing

c.halt().why: movement.walk checks a cancel only at MoveStart, the whole move before the first step, and Moved/EnterSquare are plain Events

c.halt(on=).why: MoveStart is cancellable but fires once before the walk; movement.walk's loop breaks only when step fails _clear and never re-asks can_move

c.heal_bonus().why: Healed is a Decision with a writable amount and c.half_healing is the precedent; unconfirmed whether the line needs the heal's dice, which Healed does not carry

c.heal_check().found: engine.skills ('heal' is a skill), c.check, events.SkillCheck
c.heal_check().why: The check rolls, but no action offers one in a fight so no SkillCheck with that skill is ever announced, and the event names an actor with no patient -- which is the half both rows need to tie the check to whoever was healed.

c.healing_infusion().found: cf:artificer-f2 and p4128 / p7635 / p10187, all declared
c.healing_infusion().why: Checked the registry and the item spec: cf:artificer-f2 is declared, the item's own spec names it by ref, and the three infusion cards it budgets are all declared too -- so 'one named class feature nothing models' is false and PowerUsed on those three refs is the window. Not run down: I did not read the card's payload clause, so I cannot say the whole row is writable.

c.hide(auto=).why: The worked pattern is in the tree twice: query.cover_between decides whether the creature has cover or concealment and c.hide() follows, which is the accepted simplification given no opposed Stealth roll exists. c.arm_trigger is what arms a standing permission that costs the watcher the action, which is m6344a0's stated objection.

c.hide(cover=).found: query.cover_between answers the cover half; nothing models a hide *attempt*
c.hide(cover=).why: c.hide delegates straight to c.invisible and grants the state outright, so cf:rogue-scoundrel-f1s2's 'permission to attempt a hide' has nothing to attempt: there is no Stealth-versus-Perception contest in skills.py, and granting the state on MoveEnd would be strictly stronger than the card, as the row says.

c.hide(despite_cover=).why: Hiddenness is the HIDDEN_FROM relation and the loss of cover ends it with nothing holding it open; the row was already re-pointed once off c.stay_hidden() after that need turned out to be a window instead. No candidate scored.

c.hide(partial_cover=).why: _hiding already offers the hide on cover_between(...) or concealment_of(...), partial included, and cover_between counts the target's own allies as cover

c.hide(when=).why: the row's own docstring says the check and the hide both play and the concealment gate is asked by hand in the watch

c.hit_count().why: `_hits_this_use` counts 'how many of this row's targets it has hit on this use' by walking the bus back to this row's own `PowerUsed` -- the count the symbol names, already written. f1123 keeps a separate residual the symbol does not name: the first target's damage is paid before the second hit is known, so the bonus has to be applied retroactively.

c.hit_twice().why: 'The one creature a resolved use hit with two separate attacks' is written and answers off PowerResolved.rolls, so a single use's second hit is askable. Not run down: i2981p1 may mean two hits across different uses -- check whether its printed trigger is one use or an encounter tally, which _twice cannot see.

c.host(decoy=).why: c.conjure and c.summon both make real entities that take damage, and Scenery has no Health so it cannot be attacked at all

c.host_of(ref).why: c.mount reads relations.sources(RIDDEN_BY, me) and c.ride writes it, so the board does record one creature carrying another

c.ignore_concealment().why: f1832 already corrected itself -- 'c.ignore_cover does waive the concealment -2 ... so the verb is not absent' -- so m5427a0's 'nothing reads a concealment exemption' is wrong. But cover and concealment share one Mods key and cover_waived takes the larger of two, so writing either row with the existing verb is strictly stronger than its card. What I would check: whether splitting the key into a concealment-only one is local to cover_waived and cover_between.

c.ignore_condition(redirect=).why: Both halves exist: ignore_condition suppresses a standing daze or stun without curing it, and grant_attack makes a named creature swing now at a named target. ConditionApplied announces after the condition lands, which suppression tolerates. Not run down: whether the printed 'instead' tolerates a suppress-then-force sequence, and whether the attack must be the creature's own choice (c.dominate) rather than aimed.

c.ignore_cover(concealment_only=True).why: resolve.situational takes the larger of cover and concealment and consults one waiver for the pair, so there is no concealment-only half to turn off. Both rows ran this down and refused to lay the broad waiver, which would let the creature shoot through a wall.

c.ignore_cover(reduce=).why: query.cover_waived is a threshold resolve.attack compares against, so only all or none is expressible

c.ignore_cover(reroll=).why: f2849's reasoning holds: c.ignore_cover takes a when= gate, but cover is read inside defence() with resolve's own context where reroll is always False, and the reroll's context exists only for the attack re-sum. A gate on it would be silently false rather than wrong.

c.ignore_hazards().why: m6073a0: c.resist and c.immune are about an attack's damage types and about conditions; a zone's burn and a hazard's damage reach the creature through Effect.ongoing and the zone's own tick, and nothing waives either by source.

c.ignore_insubstantial().why: the kwarg exists and its docstring is verbatim the clause, noted as printed on a handful and nowhere expressible

c.ignore_line_of_effect().found: query.line_of_effect -- the check, not a waiver
c.ignore_line_of_effect().why: line_of_effect is consulted in targeting and nothing sets it aside; c.ignore_cover is the analogous waiver and covers cover and concealment only. The read exists and the override does not.

c.ignore_requirement(ref).found: nothing (c.waive is conditions, c.counts_as is weapon requirements only)
c.ignore_requirement(ref).why: f2933 is right that the gate is asked by `dsl.usable` off the header before any body runs. `c.counts_as` relaxes a *weapon* Requirement through `Gear.counts_as` and `c.waive` relaxes a condition's costs; neither reaches a row's printed Requirement predicate, and nothing standing on a creature does.

c.ignore_resistance(below=).why: amount= is a cap and the row needs a threshold; the signature has amount, dtype, immunity and insubstantial and no comparison knob

c.ignore_run_penalty().why: actions.py:1234 gates the run's CA grant on that key and five content rows already turn it off; the attack-penalty half needs nothing, the engine never applies one

c.ignores_charge_lockout().found: components.Budget, content precedent writing Budget by hand (powers/battlemind/level_7)
c.ignores_charge_lockout().why: actions.py zeroes standard, move and minor unconditionally after a charge, but content does reach Budget directly, so restoring them from a watcher may be available. Not run down: the ordering -- whether a row's watcher can fire after actions.py has zeroed the budget.

c.ignores_difficult(hazardous=).why: 'hazardous' appears nowhere in the tree and Grid.difficult's labels are terrain words; the second clause this marker bundles is already c.waive(SQUEEZING, ...)

c.ignores_difficult(in_light=).found: nothing -- Movement.ignores is a label set
c.ignores_difficult(in_light=).why: The light half is already readable (c.unlit), so the symbol is squarely the gated ignore, and Movement.ignores is a set of strings with nowhere to hang a predicate while when= is the convention on every modifier verb. The row says 33 rows want this kwarg, which makes it the largest single one in the tree rather than a mis-mark.

c.ignores_difficult(made_by=).why: difficult terrain is word-tagged already; unconfirmed the creating rows tag their zones with any shared word

c.ignores_difficult(squares=).why: c.ignores_difficult is a set of terrain labels with a when= word, so it is all-or-nothing by construction and there is nowhere to put a count. f1873 writes the charge half exactly and explains why the partial half is a different gap.

c.ignores_difficult(while_near=).why: the verb's when= is a movement-kind string and raises outside movement.PRICED_KINDS; the exemption is a label with no predicate

c.ignores_difficult_in(who=).found: c.ignores_difficult(kind=, on=) keyed to the zone's own difficult label
c.ignores_difficult_in(who=).why: Zone.difficult may be a *string* and Zones.difficult_squares hands that label through as the terrain kind, while c.ignores_difficult takes both a kind and a creature -- so a single named enemy can be exempted from exactly one zone's ground, which is p16064's 'enemies that lack earth walk'. f1341 wants the inverse (one enemy affected, everybody else not) and that still means exempting the rest of the board.

c.ignores_squeeze_speed().why: c.waive switches off single Rules knobs without lifting the condition and its docstring names this very case: c.waive(SQUEEZING, 'halve_speed')

c.immediate_actions().why: Nothing grants a second immediate action, and m3471a4 needs one scoped to a single named row. No candidate came near.

c.immovable(except_ref=).why: movement.forced hands the forced gate {how, power} with power=self.ref, and agreed<=0 returns 0 squares, so a large gated resist is the carve-out

c.immovable(from_=).why: movement.forced returns 0 when agreed<=0 and the gate gets {how, power}, so a large gated resist is a refusal narrowed to those sources -- the f2566 shape

c.immovable(when=).why: the gate reads the shove's ctx {how, power}, ForcedMove.power exists precisely so melee or ranged can be told from a burst, and _settle clamps at max(0, ...)

c.immune(all=).why: c.immune lays one mod per named condition, and save-ends holds that are not conditions have no entry to name

c.immune(from_power=).why: query.immune_to builds ctx = {cond, target, source, power} and its comment says power was added precisely so 'immune to ... caused by a named kind of power' could be written

c.immune(keyword=).why: immunity is a Mod keyed 'immune to <condition>'; no keyword immunity is recorded. f3402 files the same gap as query.immune_to(keyword) -- retire one

c.immune(ongoing=).why: c.immune takes conditions only and Defences.immune holds damage types; nothing clears or blocks an Effect's ongoing tuple

c.immune(vs=).why: m5789a0 wants 'takes damage as normal but ignores all other effects' of attacks against one defence. Scoping a *defence bonus* by attack kind is routine (items.arms._vs_ranged), but a rider is applied by the attacking row's own body right after `c.hit()`, so there is nothing to intercept.

c.immune_keyword().why: c.immune registers one Mod per named Condition, so a keyword-tagged effect carrying no condition lands regardless; c.forbid(keyword=) is the opposite sentence

c.immune_power().found: c.forbid (takes a row away from its owner), c.immune (conditions), c.resist (damage types)
c.immune_power().why: Nothing asks 'is this creature immune to the row being used on it', and neither immunity verb takes a ref -- forbid is about the holder of a row, not its target. The temp-hp conversion needs the same absent hook.

c.improvised().why: There is no improvised weapon row in the weapon table, so the proficiency header has no ref to name and the 1d8/1d10-plus-2 line has no weapon to sit on. A data gap, and cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0 names it as one of three separate holds.

c.in_vehicle().why: Nothing puts a creature inside another one - c.shares_space covers only the square, c.ride/c.mount covers only a rider - so there is no place for the interior, the doors that cut line of sight, or the occupants who move with it. Three rows on one creature wait on it.

c.in_zone(label=).found: World.zones.all() -> zone.label / zone.owner / zone.squares; powers.warden.zone_named, level_11 _labelled_squares
c.in_zone(label=).why: m3828a4 says 'nothing can ask whether a creature is standing in somebody else's zone', but zones are enumerable with their owner, label and squares, and powers/druid/level_6_b.p5052 already walks world.zones.all() and reads zone.squares on a written row. The gate is a membership test over that, not a missing mechanism.

c.inhabit(body).why: nothing puts two creatures in one square for one blow to reach; c.merge removes the occupant from reach, the opposite of the printed line

c.initiative(fixed=).why: Encounter.adjust_initiative returns the new count so c.initiative(25 - c.initiative(0)) pins it; unconfirmed a trait arming before _roll_initiative survives the roll

c.initiative_bonus().why: i1970x1 says 'a trait is armed after the rolls, so there is no way to add to the check'. adjust_initiative handles exactly that case -- its comment says `started` is set after _arm_traits, so a trait bumping the number now re-splices the order -- and lint.py already names c.initiative(amount, on=) as the replacement for the unread 'initiative' modifier key.

c.installed(ref).why: m5641a2's Requirement is that a named installation off the board is running; `c.scenery` is map furniture inside the fight and `c.terrain` is what sort of place it is, and nothing holds a standing off-board arrangement.

c.instead_of(move=).why: p9401 reads its distance through c.squares_for so a modifier reaches it; unconfirmed because squares_for entries add where this card replaces

c.instead_of_slide().why: general_v.py:937 does exactly this; unconfirmed whether the flail rows that slide expose c.instead_of('slide', ...) -- two rows do

c.instead_of_surge().why: a refusable Decision carrying power and source -- the door c.no_surges goes through -- so a BEFORE watch can refuse the spend and then pay out with c.spend_surge

c.insubstantial(to=).why: insubstantial is a Condition plus Defences.half_except keyed by damage type; halving has no per-attacker scope

c.insubstantial(when=).why: i2426x1 refuses on the grounds that 'the damage context carries no attacker', which is stale: `dmg_ctx` has carried `source` and `from_attack` since #302, and `_scoped_vuln` already reads a predicate-gated defence off `vulnerable_when`. `insubstantial`'s own `except_`/`half_except` is where a `when` would hang, beside the halving that is read inside the same context.

c.invisible(sustain=).why: the field exists and durations reads it; unconfirmed whether setting it post-hoc on a returned effect is sanctioned, since every other sustain goes through a kwarg

c.invisible(when=).why: A re-asked, per-looker gate exists for concealment -- conceal takes a context predicate and total concealment is already aimed at one named creature -- so the distance and daze gates may be sayable that way. Not run down: whether these cards need HIDDEN_FROM's extra effects (targeting, combat advantage), because that is a relation and cannot carry a gate.

c.is_hazard().why: c.burns tags every hazard's bite detail=f'{ref} zone', but nothing marks a zone as a hazard rather than an ordinary aura, so a ' zone' read would over-match

c.is_kind(size=).why: c.size_of returns a Size off Position and kinds_of carries the type words -- two existing reads, not a missing query

c.item_charges().why: A ref-keyed counted resource with a spend and a query already exists and is the shape charges are -- Powers.per_day is a dict of ref to count. Not run down: charges have no daily reset and no printed maximum anywhere on Item, so the clock and the ceiling are genuinely absent even though the counter is not.

c.item_set().why: The module says the 15 set pages' tables 'are not theirs and are not read here at all', and each member is parsed as a separate Item row, so no set membership reaches the database. Nothing to count and nothing to ask after.

c.jump(before=).why: the body can jump then strike, so the marker's reason is false; unconfirmed is the distance -- nothing turns an Athletics check into a jump length

c.jump(no_provoke=).found: c.no_provoke(when=) with the opening's kind and mode
c.jump(no_provoke=).why: The no_provoke gate is read inside the veto and is handed "how and by what means the provoker moved" alongside actor/provoker/why (cast.py:4643), so a narrowing by kind of movement is already sayable. The obstacle is that c.jump delegates straight to c.move, so the step reads as a walk; I would check whether a jump can carry its own kind through movement.

c.jump(to=).why: away_from is already a passthrough to c.move's bias; unconfirmed that biasing away guarantees landing outside the attacker's reach

c.jump_charge().why: c.run_at walks nothing when the target is already beside the runner, so the jump covers the ground and the swing still carries charge=True

c.killed_this_turn().why: the tally is already kept in the row's own body, a Dropped watcher appending to killed; the only unwritten clause is the outright death, which c.kill now covers

c.knowledge_check().why: c.check(against=) can make an opposed check but actions.legal offers no knowledge action, so the declared SkillCheck trigger has no event

c.learn().why: c.grant_row carries no attack line and no requirement, and the printed numbers are absolutes rather than deltas

c.leash(anchor_ref=).why: anchoring to a named creature composes today; unconfirmed whether this anchor is fielded as a board entity with a readable ref at all -- may be defect=

c.leash(anchors=).why: takes exactly one to= or one square= and neither accepts a set

c.leash(every=).why: Leash is one component per creature with single radius/to/square fields, so a second c.leash overwrites the first

c.leash(forced=).why: c.forbid, c.weakened and c.suspend_when all exist; unconfirmed whether the anchor square is readable from content -- it lives in the Leash component

c.leash(per_turn=).why: Leash is a fixed radius round a fixed anchor read in movement.reachable, and nothing re-measures it at the start of a turn

c.leaves_play().why: Rules gives REMOVED cannot_act/cannot_move and both bard/level_5.py and wizard/level_10.py use it for 'removed from play' verbatim; the steering half is c.dominate

c.leaves_the_grid().why: c.merge is the near miss but needs an impassable empty square and movement.place refuses an occupied one

c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause).found: c.lend_augment(ref, cost, clause) -- the verb exists
c.lend_augment(ref_or_class, clause).why: f3170 wants to hand p10440 an Augment 1 clause it does not print, and that is the verb's stated purpose: 'Four feats print an Augment line on a card that prints none'. The marker's 'ref_or_class' asks for a whole class of rows where the row names one ref. The real proviso is the verb's own: the lent-to row must ask with augment.lent(c).

c.lend_defences().found: c.rider()/c.mount() close the other half only
c.lend_defences().why: Finding the rider is solved; substituting one creature's defence numbers for another's is not, and 'not including any temporary bonuses' rules out computing a difference and laying it as a modifier.

c.lend_skills().why: `c.passive(skill, of=other)` reads another creature's modifier (plus 10) and `c.bonus("skill:insight", 2)` is a live key -- cf:ardent-f0 lays one -- so 'use my modifier for these four skills' is the difference of the two laid as four modifiers. f30 is writable today; nothing new is needed.

c.light(square=).why: m4589a3 refuses because 'the engine has no light level', which is stale: `c.light` lays a carried `light_radius`, `query.light_level` is the reader and `Grid.light` is the painted map field (query.Light: 'absent from Grid.light means BRIGHT'). Lighting a square rather than a creature is a kwarg onto an existing model.

c.line_of_sight_from().why: measured_from traces line of sight and effect from a lender's square for ranged, area_burst and wall ranges while the lender is on the board and in sight, and cast_from holds that for a duration -- so 'nothing can move where it looks from' is no longer true.

c.lose_hp().why: every path lowering Health goes through resolve.deal_damage and emits DamageRolled/DamageApplied; c.flat(unpreventable=) is still damage

c.make_critical().why: That helper writes the critical onto the live AttackResult inside the Hit interrupt window *and* onto the event, precisely because the outcome is recomputed from the result object -- so promoting a swing is done in the tree today. f976's remaining difficulty is its own: two swings come out of one row in an order it cannot pin down, which is an ordering problem rather than a missing facility.

c.make_thrown().found: c.weapon_dice (the per-character replace(w) copy in Gear.weapons), Weapon.thrown, resolve._long_range
c.make_thrown().why: RE-JUDGED. The earlier verdict named c.as_ranged and was wrong: it said these rows want 'the same modifier without once=True', a standing 'reach' bonus. Read the cards -- f1841, f1843 and f3641 all say use this MELEE weapon as a heavy thrown weapon with a normal range of 5 and a long range of 10 (6/12 on f3641). A reach bonus cannot say that. Weapon.thrown is a separate field from Weapon.ranged on purpose -- its own comment: 'Gear.ranged means can be fired, and a dagger cannot be' -- and resolve._long_range reads the weapon's range pair, not its reach. So this is the per-character weapon write, the same mechanism as c.counts_as(property=) wants for Weapon.properties and the one c.weapon_dice already performs. The two symbols are ONE gap of 9 rows, not two of 4 and 5. Note for whoever builds it: Weapon.__post_init__ now derives hands from properties (#562), and dataclasses.replace re-runs it, so the per-character copy keeps the two fields in step for free. The three symbols c.make_thrown(), c.weapon_range() and c.counts_as(property=) are ONE mechanism over 10 distinct rows -- f1841/f1843 carry two of them and f1277 carries two. #643.

c.malfunction().why: AttackRolled carries natural and i3461x1 already watches it for ev.natural == 1 and damages the roller, the same shape this row calls unwatched

c.mark(sustain=).why: m958a3 already writes this exact shape, so a Sustain Minor mark is a sustained effect whose payout re-lays c.mark

c.mark_penalty().why: change_amount exists for precisely this sentence -- 'the size of what a mechanic grants is written inside its own body, so "you grant a +3 bonus, rather than the normal +2" had nothing to change' -- and it is how MANOEUVRE_AID is raised by seven rows. _mark_penalty returning a hard-coded 2 is the shape change_amount's docstring calls this component's commonest bug; make it read amount_for and all four rows become 'instead' rather than 'as well'.

c.max_height().why: c.height reads the distance and c.rise/c.hover set it, and nothing caps it - c.leash bounds distance from a creature or a square, not altitude. m115827a0's whole printed trait is the cap.

c.max_hp().why: f171 and f3313 both want a character's maximum raised and Health.max_hp is written only by loader and chargen -- there is no mod key for it and no content row touches it (surge_value and bloodied are derived from it, so a per-encounter hand-flip would also creep). A build-time grant, like the chargen.* symbols already judged real.

c.max_surges().why: components.py:132 holds max_surges, turns.py:704 refills to it, and a content row already writes `health.max_surges += 1` by hand in feats/paladin.py. The pool is raised and honoured; what is absent is a Cast door, which items/waist.py:848 already says in so many words.

c.maximise(dice=).why: f3610 says the listener reads damage_of(0), finds nothing and returns -- true of the DamageRolled listener and only that. c.maximise also lays a `maximise` Mod, and _roll_damage consults _take_maximum() where 'the dice are in hand', written precisely because a character's damage is rolled in the body.

c.maximise(healing=).why: c.maximise tops up DamageRolled only, and Healed carries a settled amount with no dice left

c.maximise_dice().why: c.maximise maxes the whole roll and c.change_dice replaces the expression; neither names a count of dice to max

c.merge(move_only=).why: actions.legal reads only two modifier keys and nothing narrows the menu by action kind

c.merge(on=).why: c.merge(into=, until=) takes no on= and its body moves self; nothing buries another creature or cuts line of effect both ways for somebody else

c.milestone().why: The place a milestone count would live exists -- `Sheet` even comments that 'a milestone grants more' action points -- but nothing counts encounters within a day: there is no encounter counter in `story`, and `LongRested` is defined in `events.py` and never emitted. cf:artificer-f0 under-grants deliberately for this reason.

c.min_die().found: Cast._rolled_above, Cast._reroll_floor, c.reroll_ones(below=), all inside Cast._roll_damage
c.min_die().why: A floor under each individual die is exactly what `_rolled_above` applies, per die rather than per expression, where the dice are in hand -- the same place c.maximise and reroll_damage are read. The row's premise that the dice are gone by the time anything looks is wrong.

c.mode(suspend=).why: c.mode writes max(speed, had) so it can only raise a mode; nothing takes a printed fly speed off the block

c.modify_power().why: Swapping one condition for another inside another row's zone needs a hold on that row's body, and the ref-keyed override family (change_dice, change_amount, extend_move) all require the target row to read the modifier -- there is no route that edits a row from outside it.

c.move(ends_on=).why: c.move has no destination constraint; the to=/bias parameters elsewhere name a square, not a class of legal landing squares

c.move(through=).why: _through_them covers a stated number of squares straight through whoever is in the way, reporting each creature entered once, by calling movement.overrun with the printed kind - and c.shift(share=)/c.teleport(share=) do the single occupied square. So "entering an occupied square has no verb" is stale on both counts.

c.move_before_targeting().why: dsl.use computes the target list before the Cast is constructed and before the body runs; the header offers only requires=, a read-only predicate

c.move_through().why: `_through_them` covers a stated distance straight through whoever is in the way and calls movement.overrun with the printed kind, reporting each creature entered once. p16677's rider is that call. m5431a1's residue -- squeezing through an aperture -- is a grid gap and a different symbol.

c.move_through_enemies().why: level_01/skirmishers_sa._shift_through states it outright: "'It can move through enemies' spaces' is share=True on the step rather than a waiver of anything", and level_11/skirmishers_sc._through_them covers a run straight through bodies via movement.overrun. i3441x1's 'c.phasing goes through walls, not through people' is looking at the wrong verb.

c.move_zone(conjuration=).why: c.move_zone reads world.get(zone, _Zone) and refuses anything without a Zone component, so the widening is still the gap

c.move_zone(with_me=).why: Zone.aura is the recomputed-from-owner setting; unconfirmed whether p2473's placed burst can be re-anchored, since c.move_zone refuses a zone that is already an aura

c.moved_by_me().why: in a Moved watcher it returns the Cast running now; unconfirmed whether the mover's row is always on _RUNNING -- a teleport from the action menu is not

c.movement_instead(adjacent=).why: p2105 wraps its shift and the slide into the vacated square in one c.instead_of('shift', step_and_drag) with a comment saying they are replaced together

c.movement_tax().why: Difficult terrain is a property of a square - c.zone(difficult=) and the terrain label set - and nothing charges by direction of travel or by proximity to a particular creature. All three rows reach that conclusion independently and c.slowed is the only near thing, which caps a whole move.

c.must_attack(on=, against=).why: and it is a policy/ gap rather than an engine one: c.cannot_attack only forbids, c.may only asks, and nothing instructs the chooser to take the nearest foe

c.nearest_enemy().why: policy/ has a nearest_enemy scoring feature -- same word, different layer; no rule reads it, so there is nothing to override

c.next_attack_becomes().why: i2452p1 and i1440p1 both name c.deals as 'the nearest thing' and say the only thing stopping it is that Cast._typed applies the override to weapon powers alone, so an arcane implement row is untouched. The override store and its reader exist; what I did not confirm is whether that weapon-power test is the single gate, or whether an implement row's damage is rolled somewhere _retyped is never consulted.

c.no_action_point_refresh().why: c.action_point only decrements, stamps spent_round and calls extra_action; c.restore_use is the only thing handing a use back, so there is nothing to narrow

c.no_advantage(cause=).why: query._has_combat_advantage builds a ctx of attacker/target/power and nothing else, and climbing is not even one of its branches

c.no_advantage(gains=).why: every suppressor in has_combat_advantage is read off the target's Mods while the attacker side carries only the granting key

c.no_advantage(squeezing=).why: _NEUTRAL lists grants_ca as waivable and c.waive's docstring uses squeezing as its worked example

c.no_advantage(unless=).why: _has_combat_advantage asks no_advantage first and hands the gate {attacker, target, power}; unconfirmed whether it can see a grant laid as a mod rather than the relation

c.no_augment(ref).why: dsl.affordable builds the augment forms from the point pool and the header's costs and consults no modifier

c.no_aura().why: a monster trait is an ordinary row and a zone's label is the laying row's ref, so it is nameable; unconfirmed is enumerating another creature's aura, since c.my_zones is the caster's own

c.no_basic(scope=).why: one-action-a-turn exists as a condition rule, but dazed also grants advantage and bars reactions, which the card does not print

c.no_conceal().why: its docstring is 'does not benefit from cover or concealment', it sits on whoever is looked at, and query.cover_waived reads no_cover. Residual is only invisibility, which runs on a relation

c.no_conceal_in().why: c.aura returns a zone id and c.grants_in(zid, 'no_cover', ...) routes through _while_inside to lay the exact key query.cover_waived reads

c.no_coup_de_grace().why: c.coup_de_grace consults nothing on its victim, so there is no exemption to set; i2163x1's other clause is out of combat entirely.

c.no_encounter_attacks().why: `_no_limited_attacks` already writes 'cannot use daily or encounter powers' by walking `Powers.all` and calling `c.forbid` on every non-at-will row with an attack line, ending them all off one save-ends hold. cf:assassin-f1s1 refuses on the grounds that the set would be 'a hand-listed set of refs that goes stale' -- `_arcane_rows` shows the registry filter is the answer instead.

c.no_enter(zone).found: nothing -- `no_enter` exists nowhere in the engine, only in these two content markers; Zone carries difficult, blocks_sight and obscured and no exemption
c.no_enter(zone).why: The row's premise is wrong in the harder direction: nothing bars a creature from entering a square or a zone at all, so 'except its owner' is not the missing half. Both rows need the bar itself built first.

c.no_entry().why: movement._clear/_can_stop consult no per-creature veto, so the waivers a phase or teleport grant cannot themselves be refused

c.no_invisibility().why: invisibility is HIDDEN_FROM read only by combat advantage, and see_invisible switches that branch off per watcher; looped over the caster's side it is the same team reading the row already uses

c.no_miss_damage(half=).why: deal_damage is handed a miss flag and keeps it out of the damage context, and c.no_miss_damage's docstring confirms it is 'the only thing that reads it'. Halving needs the flag where a gate can see it, which is a small engine change and not an existing facility.

c.no_miss_effect().why: the trigger is PowerResolved and nothing reaches back into a use that has finished; c.no_miss_damage is a defender-side modifier for a different sentence

c.no_mode(name).why: c.mode is itself a plain dict write plus an undo; unconfirmed whether removing a stat-block mode by hand is acceptable rather than a verb

c.no_opportunity_attacks().why: cancels OpportunityWindow in the BEFORE window for one named creature, which is exactly the narrower clause c.cannot_attack overshoots

c.no_provoke(once=).why: no_provoke is itself an interrupt on that window; unconfirmed a second watcher can end the hold after the first veto rather than before

c.no_raise().why: c.reanimate consults nothing on the corpse and no field or key records a bar on being raised

c.no_recharge().why: actions.recharge rolls its d6 and consults no Mods at all, and cast.py does not contain the word recharge

c.no_teleport().why: c.forbid's own docstring names this sentence: 'p12344's "cannot teleport" is the same sentence about a different keyword', and it takes both keyword= and lacking=, which is i2908p1's 'in both directions'. c.no_walk is the mode-barring mirror and is three lines -- a Mods key plus a reader in query.can_walk.

c.no_teleport_within().why: c.leash tethers the creature it is laid on and c.forbid(keyword=) bars its own rows; nothing refuses a teleport by where it lands

c.no_turn(who).why: c.summon's docstring says loader.spawn alone makes an entity not in the initiative order, which is exactly no turn; spawn_associate also derives hp and defences (#459)

c.no_walk(from_=).why: a leash at the current distance anchored on the attacker is read in movement.reachable, so squares increasing the distance are never offered while lateral ones still are

c.no_walk(toward=).why: query.can_walk reads mods.total('no_walk', {}) with an empty ctx and answers yes or no, so no reader carries a direction

c.obscure(level=).found: c.conceal(total=) -- the grades exist, the step-down does not
c.obscure(level=).why: conceal lays a kind='concealment' modifier at 5 (total) or 2 (partial) where the larger wins, so laying a 2 over a standing 5 changes nothing. Downgrading a concealment already in force has no expression in either the modifier path or Zone.obscured.

c.on_aegis().found: c.use_power / c.grant_row as the announcing door
c.on_aegis().why: The blocker f1156 names is purely that the three aegis rows roll their punishment inside a closure the minor-action body arms, so nothing distinguishable is emitted - and a punishment written as its own row would announce PowerUsed. That is a content restructure rather than an engine gap; I would check whether an aegis punishment can be split out without changing what it does.

c.on_any_sustain().found: c.on_sustain(effect, fn) takes any Effect; World.effects.of(who) hands the live ones back
c.on_any_sustain().why: i2900x1 says c.on_sustain only answers 'an effect this row made', but the verb takes an Effect object and appends to its on_sustain list, so another row's live hold can be bolted onto. Not run down: there is no Sustained event, so effects laid *after* the item's property arms would be missed -- which may be the whole of what the card means.

c.on_damage_die().why: DamageRolled carries a total and _roll_damage returns a sum, so the individual faces exist nowhere a row can read.

c.on_damage_reduced().why: i1834x1 is accurate: `c.reduce` takes the number off the damage and emits no event of its own, so there is no moment for a second row to answer. `DamageRolled`/`DamageApplied` announce the roll and the application, never a reduction.

c.on_death(ref).why: actions._powers skips any row carrying a Trigger line, so declaring on= would take this standard-action daily out of the menu entirely

c.on_death_save().why: turns._death_saves builds the context with label='death' and its own comment says it is there so '+2 to death saving throws' is a gate

c.on_defiling().why: Nothing in the vocabulary comes close, and the three feats record that the ability the clause rides on is in no compendium table at all -- no Power, Feat, Theme or Class -- so there is no ref to watch and no event to hook. f3190 reached this after already being re-aimed off c.class_feature().

c.on_dismiss(ref, fn).why: `c._banish` despawns a conjuration silently and `events.py` has `Summoned` and `ZoneEnded` but no dismissal event; f3189/f3200 both say the payout of a deliberate end is `c.endable(then=)`, which a row writes into its own body and a second row cannot add to.

c.on_expire().why: once=True is implemented by ending the effect, so on_end fires identically for consumption and for the clock, and on_end takes no arguments

c.on_extra_damage().why: That helper *arms* a once-per-round rider. f1114 needs a rider's payout *announced*, so an area power can copy the amount onto its other targets. The writer exists and the event does not.

c.on_feature_power().why: c.pre_empt(ref, what, clause) names a clause *inside* a row - "pull", "temp_hp", "fell_might_damage" - and hands the substitute the same Cast, which is the nearest thing in the tree to reaching a feature's internal moment. I would check whether a registered clause can run instead_of's default and add to it (riding rather than replacing), which is what f788 and f469 need.

c.on_feature_roll().why: The feature is modelled and the replacement is sayable, but the die is rolled while the trait arms and announced to nobody, so the call can only be made once the answer is known -- which would make the choice free. The missing thing is the moment, and nothing stands in for it.

c.on_flanked().why: _enemy_flanked_me is a Trigger(Moved, ...) predicate reading team, distance_between and flanked_by -- 'an enemy ends its movement in a square where it flanks it' -- and a second monster block does the same on MoveEnd. f1282b's 'nothing announces the moment it becomes true' is false; the window is a Moved watcher, and its Effect half (c.no_advantage) is already writable.

c.on_grab_attack().found: c.grab_attempt + as_="grab" on the attack events and the damage/attack ctx
c.on_grab_attack().why: c.grab_attempt rolls Strength vs Reflex with as_='grab' (#501, #510), and resolve stamps as_ into the attack ctx and onto AttackDeclared/AttackRolled/Hit -- c.bull_rush's docstring says 'as_="bull_rush" is what the 14 modifiers gate on'. So i774x1's 'a grab is an ordinary attack the engine does not label' and f2427's 'there is no roll to crit with' are both stale. m4388a3 (a bonus to dragging a held creature) is a separate manoeuvre with no as_ of its own.

c.on_granted_save().why: SavingThrow carries actor/against/natural/bonus/saved and Durations.save sets against=str(eff); nothing names who asked for the throw

c.on_granted_shift().why: MoveEnd carries actor, at and kind_ and no power (events.py:182), and f469 reports the same for Forced - so nothing says which row granted a step. query.granted_actions answers what a creature *may* do, not what a row just caused.

c.on_instinctive().found: as_= on c.attack (the grab/bull-rush label), actions._instinctives
c.on_instinctive().why: f1876 says the attack a summon makes on its own 'is announced as an ordinary attack by an ordinary creature'. The engine already has a label that rides the attack events and the ctx for exactly this kind of narrowing, and the action kind 'instinctive' exists in actions.py. Not confirmed: whether the instinctive path can thread as_ through to the summon's own attack call.

c.on_invisible().why: c.hide calls c.invisible on the same HIDDEN_FROM relation with the same label, so one event cannot say which happened and a row firing on it would answer by hiding again. The moment is the gap, not the mechanism.

c.on_invoke_shrouds().why: f3636 is accurate: `c.spend_shrouds` clears the whole count in one step and emits nothing, so 'they are not removed' has no moment to answer. `c.shroud`/`c.shrouds` read and lay them but announce no invocation.

c.on_miss_all().why: 'Every roll this use made came up short' is answerable off PowerResolved and is written three times over, so f2448's 'Miss is announced per target so it cannot be asked' is stale. Its residue -- a reroll from PowerResolved buying nothing -- is c.reroll_attack(rolls=)'s symbol, not this one.

c.on_pact_boon().found: triggers.cursed_by_me + events.Dropped, as used by features/warlock.py (cf:warlock-f1s4)
c.on_pact_boon().why: Every pact boon is a row declared `on=Trigger(Dropped, cursed_by_me, ...)` and warlock.py says 'the boons are already paid', so the moment a boon triggers is that pair of facts. cf:warlock-f1s4 already writes the printed sentence 'when your pact boon triggers' as `c.watch(Dropped, fell)` guarded by `cursed_by_me`.

c.on_points_spent().found: c.spend_points (records the spend against the row's ref), powers.augment.spent_on
c.on_points_spent().why: The spend is recorded in PowerPoints and announced only as a `Note`, so a pool reaching zero is on nobody's bus. f3322's other half is a declared `out_of_combat` trait, which is inert by design rather than missing.

c.on_power_bonus().why: Mods records a modifier's number and kind and not the act of laying one, so a bonus being granted announces nothing a row can answer. f2074's second hold (which shield) is separate and also open.

c.on_racial_bonus().found: Mods entries carry m.kind, and "racial" is a kind in use
c.on_racial_bonus().why: Mods.total buckets by kind and takes the larger of each (components.py:626), and content lays kind="racial" bonuses today (f3214), so the number exists per kind and only a read-by-kind door is absent - which would answer f3787. I would check that the racial rows actually tag their bonuses; f1863's half is a prose trait with no row either way.

c.on_racial_power().found: c.expend_row + c.restore_use, and f2830 is this row already written
c.on_racial_power().why: The _racial helper's own text says the hold is that 'the racial power is named in prose with no ref', and f2817's note says 'c.expend_row is the spending and c.restore_use is the payout, so f2830 next door is this row written out'. No hook is missing; the brief's missing ref is, which is c.race_option()'s family and build._racial_powers' territory.

c.on_reduce().found: c.reduce -- the act, with no announcement
c.on_reduce().why: c.reduce takes a number off a rolled DamageRolled and emits nothing, and the creature the payout is owed to is known only inside that callback.

c.on_return_to_play().why: f3578 is accurate: a creature that leaves the board and comes back does so through `World.spawn`, which emits `Summoned` only for a summon. Out-of-play rows exist (feats.general_u._f3463_vanish) but none announces the return.

c.on_revert().found: durations.Effects.end on the foe's form effect
c.on_revert().why: content ends other creatures' effects freely; unconfirmed a form laid by another creature carries a label matchable from that ref, since c.form takes an explicit label=

c.on_sanction().why: The event names the relation and the two creatures and not the row that set it, and every class's mark is the same relation value, so there is no way to tell which mark just landed. Nothing else announces a mark.

c.on_save().found: Trigger(SavingThrow, pred) -- items.arms.i3556p1 ships on it
c.on_save().why: i1516x1 itself says 'SavingThrow is announced before it is acted on, so the roll itself is reachable from a c.watch' and asks only for the hook plus a gate; the hook exists as a declared Trigger and i3556p1 uses it with a predicate. The gates split: f3318's condition is answerable off the standing effect (see SavingThrow.effect), i1516x1's 'which row granted the bonus' is SavingThrow.power and real, and f3470's save-against-prone is a moment that never happens.

c.on_skill_check().why: SkillCheck is a Decision announced before its modifiers are totalled and its docstring names this trigger shape; c.boost_check re-sums it

c.on_sustain(conjuration).why: c.conjure applies the hold with sustain_cost and stores conj.effect, and Effects.sustaining exists for exactly this gap

c.on_sustain(group=).why: c.on_sustain(effect, fn) holds exactly one effect, so folding several conjurations' sustains into one minor cannot be said -- and that clause is the whole value of the property, so the row is right to stay refused rather than ship the half that overcharges the wizard.

c.once_per_round_bonus().why: its latch is one round stamp for the whole effect; unconfirmed whether the printed line is once per round or once per round per enemy

c.ongoing(ends_on=).why: c.endable sets Effect.drop_cost so actions.legal offers the drop to the effect's owner for a named action; pair it with c.ongoing(until=When.ENCOUNTER)

c.ongoing(on_tick=).why: Effects._on_turn_start deals the burn with detail=str(eff) and p3273 already hangs a per-tick payout off it; five files match a burn that way

c.ongoing(stacks=).why: the highest-wins rule lives in Effects.apply, so reaching it by hand hits the same refusal; there is no override parameter

c.opportunity_from(square).why: dsl.measured_from applies c.cast_from to ranged and area attacks only, while the opportunity window is cut by movement._threatened_from from each creature's footprint

c.opportunity_instead().found: c.as_basic / Powers.instead -- near miss, already run down
c.opportunity_instead().why: Both f942 and f2607 ran this down: as_basic and Powers.instead file *refs* under a window, and a bull rush or an alchemical use is an action kind with no ref to file. Whatever closes it has to carry both, which nothing does.

c.oppose_attack().why: Nothing compares one attack roll against another - c.autohit, c.cancel and c.reroll_attack all act on the triggering roll without exposing a number to beat. i2019p1's second half (c.basic(harmless=)) is independently absent.

c.opt_in().found: c.pre_empt + c.instead_of / c.instead_of_now, used by the _riders helper in the same file
c.opt_in().why: f1099's clause is 'you can forgo X to instead Y', and pre_empt registers exactly that against a named row's clause, read back 'offered, never imposed' -- general_g's own _riders helper calls c.pre_empt(on_ref, what, swap). f1021 is the one that stays: its trade is on every implement attack rather than on a named row, so there is no (ref, what) to register against.

c.overrun(at=).why: c.overrun(to=) routes through movement.reachable with no mode parameter, and c.moving_as is a query -- so this row's bare c.moving_as call is inert, worth filing separately

c.overrun(during_charge=).why: Both rows need a trait to rewrite how a charge *moves*, and actions.perform builds a charge out of a walk plus use(charge=True) before any trait sees it. c.overrun only works for the row making the move, which a trait is not; nothing in Cast reaches into the engine's own action handling.

c.overrun(squares=).why: movement.overrun walks _line(here, to) and never consults speed, so a destination from reachable_squares(me, speed//2) bounds the trample

c.oversized().why: The Weapon dataclass has ref/slug/damage/proficiency/reach/ranged/thrown/group/category/hands/properties/enhancement and no size field, and nothing refuses a weapon for being too big, so the permission has nothing to permit.

c.pact_boon().why: The boons are declared rows - features/warlock.py grants cf:warlock-f1c10 for the star leg and writes cf:warlock-f1s4's outright - so i2305p1's "nothing models the boon" is stale and c.pre_empt is what suppresses or replaces a named clause. i2343p2's "there is no bonus to add to" needs f1c10's hardcoded `c.bonus("attack", 1)` read through c.amount_for, which is one content line.

c.pass_on(attack=).found: nothing (c.pass_on handles conditions, c.redirect only an undeclared attack)
c.pass_on(attack=).why: p16049 wants a miss handed on to a creature already swapped with, after the attack resolved; `c.redirect` explicitly only re-aims one still being declared and `c.pass_on` moves a condition. Nothing re-aims a settled attack.

c.passes_through().why: overrun walks a creature through occupied squares and shuffles it into a free square at the end -- the printed 'must end its movement in an unoccupied square' -- which is both halves of what m884a4 asks for, including the refusal to stop there.

c.passive_only().why: skills.passive is 10 + modifier(...) and modifier's ctx carries only actor, skill and target, so no when= can tell a passive read from a rolled one

c.penalty(on_attacker=).why: resolve._mods(world, attacker, "attack", ctx) reads the *attacker's* own Mods, so a penalty imposed by the defender has nowhere to sit. The row also rules out the near miss (laying it on every enemy at arming misses anything that joins later) and f217 next door proves the holder-side version already works.

c.penalty(through_zone=).why: c.grants_in reaches creatures standing in a zone, and no context carries the geometry of an attack traced through one

c.permit_charge().found: nothing to build - the permission already holds
c.permit_charge().why: m5303a0 looked in actions.charge and can_walk and found nothing refusing a charge to a burrowing creature, so there is no restriction to lift. This is a row whose printed trait is already true, not a facility anybody should implement.

c.phasing(porous=).why: 'porous' exists nowhere in the engine, and the sibling marker c.conjure(porous=) names the same absent distinction from another direction

c.phasing(when=).found: c.phasing / c.mode, Movement.ignores_when (the per-kind-of-going precedent), c.suspend_when
c.phasing(when=).why: f3116 says the verb exists and 'what it has no form of is a gate'. Movement.ignores_when shows the engine keying a waiver to one kind of going, which is half the gate the card prints. Not run down: modes are resolved by movement.mode_of rather than read through Mods with a ctx, so there is no lambda to hang 'while a named racial power is unspent' on.

c.pick_roll().why: c.boost_roll adds to a roll and c.change_dice says which die; nothing reaches into a finished roll to set its face

c.pick_up().why: cf:swordmage-f0 says 'nothing anywhere picks one back up'. _picking_up is in the action menu as a minor action and its docstring names docs/blocked.json's cf:swordmage-f0 as the line that noticed. The row's second want, Gear.owned, is still real -- this symbol is not.

c.power_range().why: i2962x1 and i2771x1 say only 'a row's reach is header data and nothing lengthens another row's', which _stretched has answered since it began taking the row being measured as a gate -- the same evidence as c.reach_of(power=), and powers/sorcerer/level_6_t3 and level_2_t3 are the shipped examples.

c.prone(dc=).why: c.prone takes held: When and no difficulty; standing is priced in actions.legal with no modifier on it

c.prone(save_ends=).why: a SavingThrow whose against names prone is already produced in the tree; unconfirmed any row knocking a character prone offers one, so the feat may arm and never fire

c.prone_square().why: the composition reads right; unconfirmed whether relocating a creature in the instant the prone lands resolves cleanly

c.provoke(allies=).why: it opens a window by hand with no side test so the inversion is writable; unconfirmed because nothing announces 'an ally would have provoked'

c.provoke(ignore_reach=).why: from_ moves where the swing comes from with reach measured from there; unconfirmed whether the window c.provoke opens can be made to swing from the beast's square

c.provokes(when=).why: c.provoke opens one window now and c.no_provoke(when=) is the only standing form; there is no additive counterpart

c.provokes_from().why: 'open an opportunity window for a named creature against a target' is the whole price half, and feats.general_r._provokes_on_standing is the same call aimed the other way

c.quarry(nearest=False).found: nothing -- c.quarry measures from the ranger only
c.quarry(nearest=False).why: The nomination takes no second anchor, and cf:ranger-f0s1's other half is blocked behind the companion never taking a turn (#212), so even a kwarg would leave the feature half-dead.

c.race_components().why: f443 scales a payout by how many of a race's components the character carries. `c.race_of` and `Build.race` give the race, and nothing anywhere records per-race components as a countable thing a creature holds.

c.race_option().found: chargen.choices.race_options -- and it is the wrong thing
c.race_option().why: The top-ranked candidate ranks *races* for a class. f1521 needs which of five sub-options *within* a race is current, and says why c.element cannot stand in: two of the five are not damage types. The largest symbol in the queue and a genuine gap.

c.race_option(damage_type=).why: Build.choices emits race:<ref> but a race has no leg the way a class does, so which option within the race was taken is recorded nowhere (#235/#505)

c.racial_power_used().found: a racial row's own header (cls="r1", "r2", ...), query.race_of and c.race_of, events.PowerUsed (carries the ref)
c.racial_power_used().why: Which refs belong to a race is header data already -- every racial power is declared with the race as its class -- so the watch can ask dsl.get(ev.ref).cls rather than hand-listing three refs and going stale on the fourth, which is the only reason this row says it cannot be written.

c.racial_row().why: `_named_traits` already swaps '<name> racial trait' for '<ref> racial trait' and `rt:` refs are real rows, so the mechanism exists; f2472 and i2301x1 report that their particular grant 'names it in prose' and the spec gives no ref. Check those two against the `rt:` index and `_named_traits`' coverage -- this looks like a miss in the swap rather than its absence.

c.raging().why: both readers answer off a label; unconfirmed whether displacing the barbarian's real rage is acceptable for 'considered to be raging'

c.raise_bonus().found: c.change_amount / c.amount_for -- and m1031a4 is in the registry
c.raise_bonus().why: Both stated holds are gone. Checked the registry: m1031a4 *is* declared, so there is a bonus standing to be raised; and change_amount exists for 'make a named mechanic hand out a different number', with amount_for as the read half. The remaining work is making m1031a4 read amount_for, which is the contract that family documents.

c.raise_defence(ev=).why: re-declared on Hit, c.boost_roll(-2) recomputes result.hit from the untouched natural, arithmetically identical to +2 defence against that one attack; batch_a.py:1285 already boosts negatively

c.range_to().why: query.distance is geometry and reads no modifier at all, and nothing in the movement or targeting path consults a per-creature distance scale. Halving a measured distance has nowhere to be stored.

c.rattling(when=).why: lays its bonus and passes no when=, so the keyword half cannot be narrowed while the penalty half can -- the disagreement the row refuses to create

c.reach(set=).why: dsl._stretched reads the reach modifier on every melee range (#533: 1,023 rows plus the basic attack), which is how c.as_ranged and c.threatens both work

c.reach_bonus().why: f1995 says 'nothing rewrites it for a creature', which is flatly contradicted: _stretched exists because 'the target's reach increases by 1' and 'add your Wisdom modifier to the range of your ranged powers' were stored and never consulted, and a dozen content rows now lay those keys (ardent/level_2_t1 lays both). m6579a1's reach that follows a state is a gate lambda, since a modifier's gate is read at use time.

c.reach_of(power=).found: c.reach(ref) reads a range; the three real gaps are c.as_melee(ref=), events.PowerAimed, and nothing at all
c.reach_of(power=).why: The symbol named no verb -- Cast.reach_of has never existed, though dsl._reach_of's docstring still refers to it. Six rows carried it wanting three different facilities, so it could not go green or red correctly for any. The earlier verdict pointed at c.bonus("range", when=), which is the WRITER; what the rows needed was a reader, and c.reach(ref) has answered a ranged row's range throughout. Applied: f1817 needed no facility at all (its clause belongs in p9501, #550); f1028 and its three riders want c.as_melee(ref=); p14125 wants a moment after a range is known and before a power is aimed. Writing f1817 also exposed that p9501's ring included the creature it was centred on, so the row re-attacked the creature it missed and the ring never mattered.

c.reanimate(dominated=).why: c.dominate lays DOMINATED_BY and the condition together and names a master; the card's basic-attacks-only is a separate gap, the one c.restrict_actions names

c.reappear(after=).why: A thirty-day return has no clock: the engine's longest duration is the encounter and chargen says persistence does not exist. Narrative rather than mechanical.

c.reappear(at=).why: Condition.REMOVED only sets cannot_act/cannot_move, and c.teleport with no to= puts the destination through the decider, covering both printed branches

c.recall_weapon().why: f612 says picking a weapon off the floor 'landed this session, but that is adjacency' -- and the only range in that path is `where.square not in here` inside `_picking_up`. The state change (append to `gear.weapons`, `gear.wield`, despawn the Item) already works; a recall at twenty squares is the same three lines without the adjacency test.

c.recast(no_provoke=).why: A creature-level 'your ranged and area attacks do not provoke' is written for an armour item, so a no-provoke may be lendable for the length of one use instead of living in Power.no_provoke. Not run down: whether the provoke test reads a creature modifier or only the header.

c.recast(reach=).why: dsl._stretched reads Mods.total(key, ctx) and area_of hands it ctx={"power": p.ref, "kind": ...}, so c.bonus("blast_size", n, when=lambda ctx: ctx.get("power")==ref) widens one named row today -- f287, f601 and f1010 are writable (f1010's own docstring already found c.widen_areas). Two caveats: _stretched clamps with max(0, ...) so f2202's narrowing is still unsayable, and f725/f2819 change the range *kind* (close burst to area burst), which no modifier does.

c.recast(usage=).why: c.recast changes what a row costs; nothing changes how often it may be used. c.restore_use hands a spent use back and c.forbid takes a row away, but no modifier moves a row between usage classes. f3292's other hold (Target.square) is separate and also open.

c.recast(when=).why: that header field is a recharge condition that is a state, not a moment, re-asked at the start of the turn, which is this clause exactly; query.hidden_from takes (world, eid)

c.recharge_roll().why: no event announces a recharge roll, so c.boost_roll has nothing to attach to

c.redirect(dtype=).why: m4229a4 does the shape; unconfirmed whether that path carries the card's 'effects and secondary attacks are also deflected'

c.redirect(ev=).why: c.redirect moves ev.target with no fresh roll and never recomputes result.target_defence

c.redirect(recheck=).why: moves ev.target and result.target and never re-rolls; resolve.attack only re-announces when result.hit flips

c.redirect_damage().why: f3702's own docstring names the gap: "c.pre_empt(ref, clause) is that window and 29 rows wait on it" - and both halves are on Cast now (cast.py:6769 and :6864), with each registration becoming its own action-menu entry. "Instead takes ongoing damage equal to what you would have dealt" is a registered substitution for the damage clause.

c.redirect_miss_damage().why: c.redirect moves the whole attack before it lands and c.pass_on moves conditions not damage; the choice has to be made inside p997

c.regain_points().why: p16440 says 'c.spend_points only takes them', but transfer_points already writes `theirs.points += gone` on a PowerPoints pool and PowerPoints.refresh sets points back to maximum. Handing points back needs a one-way door onto a write the engine already makes.

c.regain_surge(until=).why: a When.ENCOUNTER hold whose on_end gives the surge back; end_encounter ends every live effect and on_end fires for every end alike, the channel m6572a2 uses

c.regeneration(add=).why: that verb is the engine's make-a-named-mechanic-hand-out-a-different-number; the missing work is in p2483's body, which hard-codes c.regeneration(2)

c.regeneration(suppressed_by=).why: unless= 'reads state at the moment of the tick' and is documented as the printed 'its regeneration does not function that turn' shape; _regenerates takes a doused label and skips the tick while a hold with that label stands, and level_11/controllers_sa.py:3612 calls it with one. m2068a3's 'there is no flag anywhere for this to flip' is the flag.

c.regeneration(when=).why: that kwarg reads state at the moment of the tick and is documented as the printed shape distinct from c.suspend_when

c.reload().why: m6507a0 and f396 both say loading is not a cost the engine charges at all, and `engine/ammunition.py` confirms it: a piece is drawn automatically when a ranged attack is declared and no action is ever spent. There is nothing to make cheaper.

c.remove_from_play().why: m6092a2 says there is 'no primitive for taking a creature off the board and bringing it back'. Condition.REMOVED exists with Rules(cannot_act, cannot_move) and _f3463_vanish is a working 'out of play until the start of your next turn'. Caveat: REMOVED does not lift the body off the grid, so an untargetable version may still be owed.

c.replace_roll().found: c.reroll_attack (writes AttackResult.natural/total), c.treat_roll_as (writes parity on the result), SavingThrow and SkillCheck are Decisions announced before being acted on
c.replace_roll().why: All three kinds of d20 are rewritable before they are honoured, so a stored face may go through the same path reroll_attack uses with a fresh die. Not run down: whether hit and critical recompute from a written `natural` outside the interrupt window, which is the whole reason treat_roll_as refused to fake the die.

c.reroll_attack(all_targets=).why: f715 was already re-pointed here (#496): `c.reroll_attack` rerolls the triggering roll off `c.trigger`, and an area power's other rolls are resolved before this fires and are not carried on the event. There is no second roll to find.

c.reroll_attack(ev=).found: c.reroll_attack (rewrites AttackResult.natural and total, honouring second-roll modifiers)
c.reroll_attack(ev=).why: The arithmetic works and only the event is unreachable, so handing a watcher's own event in is a thin door for p12321. Not run down: whether the watcher's event carries `result` -- and i2068p1/i3280p1 want a reroll banked for a later attack, which the verb cannot do at all and is a separate gap.

c.reroll_attack(rolls=).why: By PowerResolved every miss has already resolved, so a roll turned into a hit buys no damage and no rider -- the whole set has to be rerolled and what each new number lands replayed, which nothing does. p10354 and i1675p1 reached this independently and i1675p1 settled for the narrower rule.

c.reroll_attack(standing=).why: c.reroll_attack reads the attack off c.trigger, a Cast field; a watch callback is handed the event instead and cannot hold the reroll open

c.reroll_attacks_against().why: c.reroll_attack reads off c.trigger, so it can only answer a roll this creature is being offered -- it cannot make an enemy reroll, and there is no standing roll-twice modifier for attack rolls. The damage side has exactly that (c.reroll_damage with c._rolls_twice_higher, and c.damage_disadvantage laid on another creature), which is good evidence the attack-side twin is genuinely absent rather than misnamed.

c.reroll_check(standing=).why: c.arm_trigger is precisely a reaction left lying in wait for a duration that charges the watcher the action a trigger costs - which is the "once per such check" half - so p16650's "none of them can be left lying in wait" is doubtful. What I would check is whether c.reroll_check can be handed the event rather than reading c.trigger; seven sibling verbs (c.unsave, c.autohit, c.halve, c.reduce, ...) already take an explicit ev=.

c.reroll_crit_die().found: c.reroll_damage and c.reroll_ones are the near misses, both wrong
c.reroll_crit_die().why: i2299x1 wants the second roll kept, and reroll_damage keeps the higher ('the opposite of what is printed') while reroll_ones replaces only dice under a floor. Both are read in _roll_damage as mod keys, so the shape is there, but no key means 'take the second result' and the critical rider itself is applied by engine/equipment.py from an item column.

c.reroll_damage(keep=).why: The keep= vocabulary exists on both roll-again siblings, and reroll_damage already works by laying a 'damage_twice_higher' key read in _roll_damage. Not run down: a 'keep the new result' variant needs a third branch there -- would check _roll_damage reads a second key cleanly.

c.reroll_damage(ones=).why: exists and is documented as exactly 'reroll each damage die that shows a 1', read inside _roll_damage. Residual gap is only the bloodied gate, c.reroll_ones(when=)

c.reroll_damage_dice().why: All four rows argue only against c.reroll_damage (roll the expression twice, keep the higher) and none mentions c.reroll_ones, which is the other mechanic: each low die is replaced individually, the new face stands, and it is read inside _roll_damage where the dice are in hand. below= is the threshold and ref=/keyword= are the narrowings these cards print. What a count= would add is 'as many dice as you like' rather than 'the low ones'.

c.reroll_damage_once().why: c.reroll_damage lays a standing hold with no once= passthrough, and c.bonus(key, once=True) raises outright for that key

c.reroll_initiative(keep=).found: c.reroll_attack / c.reroll_save / c.reroll_check, all of which take keep=
c.reroll_initiative(keep=).why: Three of the four d20 rerolls take keep: str = "new" and implement {"new", "best", "worst"} with the same two-line dict; reroll_initiative is the only one without. i2966p1's own docstring already says keep="best" is 'what every other reroll on Cast already understands' -- the convention is there and the kwarg is not.

c.reroll_ones(group=).why: _reroll_floor reads keyword-qualified keys but not weapon-group; the row's stated reason is wrong, _rolled_above does replace each low die individually

c.reroll_ones(sneak=).why: c.reroll_ones exists, is read inside _roll_damage "where the dice are in hand", and its ref= narrows to one row's dice - so f3749's "c.reroll_damage rolls the whole thing twice instead" is stale. The striker rider's roll carries detail='cf:rogue-scoundrel-f4' (quoted in c.hide's docstring), which is the ref the sneak= kwarg was asking for.

c.reroll_ones(when=).found: c.reroll_ones is c.bonus underneath, and c.bonus takes when=
c.reroll_ones(when=).why: The verb's body is `self.bonus(what, below, on=who, until=until, stacks=False)` and Mods.total applies each modifier's gate, so plumbing when= through is the whole change; f2705's two conditions (rage.in_rage, c.wielding) are closures that need no context at all. i3374x1's combat-advantage clause is the exception -- _reroll_floor calls Cast.total with no ctx, so a gate about the target has nothing to read.

c.reset_trap().why: `Trap.sprung` is a documented field whose own comment reads 'a pressure plate that has gone off and not reset', and `terrain.arm`'s `EnterSquare` watcher fires again the moment it is false. Resetting is one field write onto a component built to anticipate it.

c.reshape_area().why: widen_areas grows a burst and move_zone carries a shape elsewhere; turning one shape into another around a fixed square is a third operation, and i1836x1 adds that a row's reach is header data.

c.reshape_weapon().found: c.weapon_dice (writes the per-character `replace(w)` copies in Gear.weapons)
c.reshape_weapon().why: 'Weapon is a column set no body rewrites' is stale: weapon_dice rewrites one character's own copy, absolutely and with no reader needed, and group and dice are fields on the same object. Becoming a different weapon is that write with two more fields.

c.resist(once=).found: c.resist's own gated path, which already delegates to c.bonus(once=)
c.resist(once=).why: When when= is passed, c.resist returns self.bonus(what, amount, kind=f"{ref} resist", when=when) -- and c.bonus already takes once=, documented as 'the bonus ends after the first attack that could use it', spent by watching the roll. 'Against a single attack' is that kwarg forwarded one level; c.conceal and c.ignore_cover already forward it the same way.

c.resist_from().why: p16372 says 'the damage context carries power but no attacker'. That is stale: #302 added `source` (who is dealing it) plus `from_attack` to dmg_ctx for exactly this sentence, and resist_ctx is `{**dmg_ctx, ...}`. c.resist already takes when=, so the gate is writable now.

c.resist_in(when=).why: the gate exists one layer down and c.grants_in already passes one through; unconfirmed whether DEAFENED is the accepted stand-in for who can hear you

c.restore_use(item=).why: The engine appears to model no item consumption at all outside a weapon/consumable flag on Gear, so it is not clear there is an expended item to hand back. If a consumable's power is an ordinary row with a use, c.restore_use(ref) already is this whole row - that is the one thing I would check.

c.restrict_action().why: conditions.py already carries a condition whose entire effect is 'No standard actions. A shape you assume rather than a thing done to you -- it still moves, and it still acts otherwise', which is i3479p1's 'cannot take a standard action' and m5449a0's dormant clause without PETRIFIED's helplessness. Encounter.can_spend reads the Budget slots, and m193a3 already writes one from content, so narrower bars are reachable too.

c.restrict_actions().why: Encounter._one_action enforces it; over-strong because dazed also carries no_reactions and c.waive accepts only four words

c.restrict_shift().why: c.leash is the only destination restriction and is read in movement.reachable for every move alike, so it would also bar the walk this card allows
