c.restrict_targets().why: c.cannot_attack(against=) bars one named creature and c.forbid one row; nothing narrows the permitted set to a single creature and there is no reader for it

c.retarget().why: `c.transfer` moves a live hold to another creature but 'refuses a hold carrying a relation or a subscription and returns None' -- which is exactly m976a2's sustained grab, a relation with an `on_sustain` subscription. Nothing re-aims a standing effect at a new target.

c.retarget(power=).why: a target line is read by dsl.candidates before the body runs, and pre_empt/instead_of only replace a clause the row itself reads

c.retarget_side().why: a row's target side is header data read before the body; c.add_target only adds a creature

c.retrieve().why: the chain exists, but c.disarm lands the weapon in the holder's own square, so nothing puts a thrown weapon where the card says it lands

c.retrieve(consumable=).why: i2067x1's premise is wrong -- drawing *is* an action the engine spends (actions._wielding charges the printed minor) and c.draws_free(only=) already makes it free for a named ref. Not run down: Gear holds weapons, so a consumable has nothing to be drawn, which may be the real gap.

c.retrigger(ref).why: f2091 widens another row's printed Trigger. `on=Trigger(...)` is header data read by the dispatcher before any body runs, and `pre_empt`/`instead_of` substitutes *body clauses* only -- nothing edits a header for one character.

c.returns_to_hand().why: c.draw takes a stowed weapon up for nothing; unconfirmed the clause has any case, since nothing models a throw removing the weapon from Gear.main

c.retype().found: c.deals / Cast._retyped (a held override that beats a printed type), f1646's DamageRolled mutation keyed on a ref
c.retype().why: An override for a duration exists and is read in the damage path, but it is keyed to the creature's WEAPON or IMPLEMENT rows rather than to one named row. Not run down: whether m3378a5's attack carries one of those keywords, in which case c.deals is the row today; if not, the f1646 watcher pattern is the fallback.

c.retype_damage(dtypes=).found: f1646's DamageRolled/Window.BEFORE mutation of ev.dtypes keyed on ev.detail, c.counts_as_keyword (+ Powers.granted_keywords, read in dsl.keywords_of)
c.retype_damage(dtypes=).why: Both halves f1231 calls missing sit in the tree: a feat beside it already adds a second type to another named row's damage, and a keyword can be granted per creature per row -- 'header data no trait can add to' is what counts_as_keyword exists to work around. It does not answer f1639/f1659, whose rider rolls no damage to catch.

c.revives_unless(within=).why: c.revives_unless implements nothing -- it writes Undying for the policy; the rising is _revives_once's own watchers, and the twin is findable with Ident.ref as m3997a1 does

c.roll_gate().why: resolve.attack recomputes the outcome from result after announcing the roll; unconfirmed because c.boost_roll reads c.trigger and this row is a trait, so it would be a hand-written watch

c.roll_twice().why: A standing 'roll twice and take the better' held on the creature and consulted as the dice come up already exists on the damage side, which is the mechanism this row describes wanting. Not run down: p16678's own note implies the card is not about damage, and which roll it *is* about decides whether this is a one-line sibling or a real gap.

c.roll_with(ability=).why: skills.py reads mods.total('ability_check', ctx) with ctx['ability'] in hand, which gates the delta onto Strength checks exactly

c.rolled_maximum().why: c.maximise's docstring says _max_of computes the ceiling and is private, and both it and c.reroll_ones are read inside _roll_damage "where the dice are in hand" - so the comparison i1577x1 wants is available at exactly the site two verbs already use. I would check whether DamageRolled can be flagged there.

c.run().why: There is no run action: actions.legal offers power, move, shift, charge, stand, escape, second_wind and the rest, and running is on none of its branches. Three of the five rows name actions.legal directly and agree.

c.running_start().found: powers.monk.second_card_1._running_jump -- a per-row calculation, not a flag
c.running_start().why: rt:r51-t1 needs a standing 'always considered to have a running start' and c.jump takes a number of squares and nothing else; _running_jump just hands it a bigger number itself. No mod key or Movement field is consulted by c.jump, so there is nothing for a trait to be true of.

c.save(against_trap=).why: effects are walkable and against= takes a label fragment; unconfirmed that an effect a trap laid carries the trap's eid as Effect.source

c.save(any_duration=).why: c.end_effect(save_ends=True) collects only When.SAVE_ENDS holds and ends them without rolling; nothing grants a throw against a fixed duration

c.save(conditions=).why: c.save filters only on 'ongoing' or a label fragment; c.end_effect has the condition pool filter but never rolls, so the logic is in the wrong verb

c.save_against_prone().why: three in-tree helpers implement exactly this from c.watch(ConditionApplied) + c.save(bare=True) + c.cure(PRONE)

c.save_disadvantage().why: The roll-twice-keep-lower pattern exists imposed on another creature for damage, laid as a modifier and read at the roll site. Not run down: durations.save is where a saving throw is rolled -- would check it can consult such a key.

c.save_order().why: Effects._on_turn_end rolls save-ends holds at TurnEnd and nothing moves the moment. i499x1 notes the keyword half is already answerable through keywords_of, so the whole remaining benefit is the timing.

c.save_to_avoid(Condition.PRONE).why: four content helpers already write this, which refutes the row's claim that no hook offers a throw as the condition arrives

c.save_vs_forced().why: i2494x1 is accurate: forced movement is shortened by `c.resist_forced` or refused by `c.immovable` and is never saved against, so there is no throw for a bonus to attach to.

c.scenery(size=).why: c.scenery returns entity ids and scenery carries a Position with a size -- c.control reads pos.size off exactly these entities

c.second_initiative().why: `_double_turn` is already 'an elite or solo acting twice a round: a spliced second initiative slot', written as `c.extra_turn(init.rolled + 10)` and described as 'the shape m192a0 already settled'. m5553a0/m5719a0/m2069a2 all refuse on the grounds that `c.extra_turn` takes a count rather than rolling a second die -- a fidelity quibble about where the second slot sits, not a missing facility.

c.see_from(square).why: c.cast_from names a creature and moves only where ranged and area attacks are measured from; every sight question still reads squares(world, eid)

c.see_from(who).why: Borrowing another creature's square for line of sight and effect is written and held for a duration, so the attack-relevant half of this row exists. Not run down: measured_from is the only reader of the borrow and it covers ranged, area_burst and wall only, so whether melee reach and perception also need to honour it decides how much is left.

c.see_invisible(within=).why: the flag is read through mods.total('see_invisible') with no radius, unlike c.truesight and c.blindsight, and the narrowing is a radius round a companion

c.set_build().why: Build.choices is written once when the character is built; cast.py touches Build in three places and all three read. Nothing puts a character on another class's leg at runtime, which is precisely what the granted options' own `if not c.build(...)` gates need.

c.set_defence().found: query.defence(world, eid, d, ctx), c.bonus(when=, once=True)
c.set_defence().why: 'Your Fortitude equals 25 against that attack' is readable as a delta: `query.defence` returns the live value including level, mods and conditions, and `c.bonus(FORT, 25 - that, when=<this attack>, once=True)` scopes it -- the gated-modifier pattern `cf:ardent-f0` and m3842a3 both use. Nothing needs an absolute-set field.

c.set_hp().why: Health.max_hp is written in exactly one place in Cast -- c.reanimate, which needs a corpse -- and nothing sets a living creature's maximum to a computed number

c.set_origin(by=).why: cast_from is this card: 'determine line of sight and effect for your ranged and area attacks from the target rather than from yourself', held standing, read in dsl.measured_from so the borrowed square decides what may be aimed at as well as where the line is traced -- and its docstring names 'the stat block trait that says the same thing about a servant'. Laid on the sibling with who=this creature, it is the printed sentence.

c.share_health(who).why: Health has no link to another creature's pool and nothing reads one

c.share_senses().why: sight lives in per-creature modifier keys read off the looker; c.cast_from moves a ranged origin only

c.share_space().why: f3670's "two creatures in one square is not a thing the grid allows" is stale: c.shares_space is the standing property that makes a square enterable and reads back through movement.shares_space, and share= is the per-move form. The gate the benefit hangs on can be true and can be asked.

c.shares_space(always=).found: movement.shares_space (a creature-level Mods key, already blanket), c.shift(share=True), c.overrun
c.shares_space(always=).why: m5808a0's claim that 'c.shares_space pairs the caster with one named creature' is wrong -- it lays a standing per-creature flag that lets anybody in. But it is the *occupant* side, and this card wants standing permission for the *mover*, which exists only per move (share=True) because movement._occupied asks the occupant and never the mover. What I would check: whether _occupied could read a mover-side key, and where the size test would live.

c.sheathed().why: Gear.stowed is an unordered set written only by chargen, and actions.py offers a draw action with no sheathe action at all

c.shift(into_space=).why: c.shift takes share: bool = False for exactly this, documented in monsters.level_04.skirmishers_sa._shift_into

c.shift(path=).why: movement.shift goes straight to the destination without checking squares between, so the pass-through already happens; unconfirmed that reconstructed line is the path the rules mean

c.shift(pulls=).why: share= only lets the mover land on an occupied square, and the nearest alternative, c.slide(to=), is forced movement this card is not

c.shift(swap=).found: c.swap, c.shift(share=True) -- neither is the rule
c.shift(swap=).why: m4617a0 needs the *destination rule* for every shift the creature makes changed; c.swap trades two squares on demand and share= lets a step pass through an occupied one. Nothing hangs a narrowing on a future shift.

c.shift(through=).why: `_through_them(c, squares_, kind="shift")` already covers a stated number of squares straight through whoever is in the way, calling `movement.overrun` with the printed kind, and exists because 'five cards here print a *shift* of a stated length through enemies' spaces'. f3320's objection is about `share=True`, which is the wrong lever rather than the missing one.

c.shift_as(when=).why: shift_as and grant_action lay a '<what> as <cost>' bonus that actions reads while building the menu, and that read passes no context

c.shift_as_teleport().found: Powers.pre_empts ('p10439's shift is replaced by two of them'), feats.battlemind_b._f3286_teleport and _f3290_teleport
c.shift_as_teleport().why: Substituting a teleport for a named row's shift is written and chosen as a variant before the shift happens, which is this card's 'instead' without needing an interrupt. Not run down: whether i2654x1 names a row or means any shift the creature makes, which pre_empts cannot key on.

c.shift_becomes_move().why: A shift a row grants is taken inside that row's body with the number in hand, and nothing intercepts one -- the same finding feats/exploits.py reached independently for f980's 'move 3 instead of 2' riders, which it marked c.movement_instead(squares=).

c.shift_becomes_teleport().why: feats/battlemind_b._f3286_teleport is this exact clause for p10439, which reads it with c.instead_of('shift', ...); p7443's body needs the same one-line read

c.shift_through_enemies().why: share=True is a permission on one step passed by the caller; movement._occupied consults only the occupant's shares_space

c.shift_while_prone().why: actions._movement returns empty for a prone creature before the shift branch, so the kinds of movement are off together. c.waive is the nearest verb and its word list is deliberately closed to four Rules fields - attack, halve_speed, grants_ca, speed_cap - with an unrecognised word raising rather than being accepted.

c.sight_range(only=).why: sets a distance; nothing restricts what a creature may see to one named creature

c.sight_range(shared_only=).why: per-pair visibility exists and c.can_see consults it, but c.see_invisible's docstring states nothing gates targeting on line of sight

c.silence().why: i3470p1: 'sound is not modelled, so the zone would be an empty shape'. Nothing in zones, query or conditions represents noise or hearing -- the only sensory model is light and line of sight.

c.skill_circumstance().why: SkillCheck carries actor, skill, total, success and bonus, and skills.check takes skill, dc, who and bonus - no target and no purpose anywhere. f946 names both halves exactly and i693x1 confirms a check's context has no room for "against one sort of creature".

c.sleeping().why: nothing records that a creature might be asleep and no event marks the state

c.slowed(mode=).why: m6608a1 and m6610a1 agree and the engine agrees with them: slowed is a Conditions.Rules speed_cap on the creature, Movement.modes is a flat dict of mode to speed, and a speed modifier means every mode at once (general_h.f1337 says so). There is no per-mode cap and c.ignore_condition would make the creature immune instead.

c.spare_death_trait().why: Dropped is a plain Event with a single emitter and only Decision subclasses carry cancel

c.speed_of(while_charging=).why: The attack context carries `charge`, so a damage- or attack-side gate on charging is already writable. Not run down: speed is read during movement rather than from an attack context, so whether a 'speed' modifier can see that key is the thing to check.

c.speed_while_squeezing().why: c.waive's own worked example is this sentence, and SQUEEZING's Rules carries halve_speed, attack=-5 and grants_ca, all three waivable

c.spend_points(choice=).why: p2482 reads c.squares_for(c.ref, 3) with the comment 'so f1236 can lengthen it', and dsl.py:2711 confirms PowerUsed fires this feat before the body runs

c.spend_surge(unless=).why: c.spend_surge is literally spend a surge and gain nothing for it, and c.on_attack watches AttackDeclared, which carries target, with no default attacker

c.split().why: m1981a3 wants one creature to become two independent bodies sharing an initiative count. `c.summon`/`c.conjure` put new entities on the board but nothing divides an existing creature or shares its slot.

c.split_weapon().why: Gear holds a list of Weapon profiles and c.as_weapon appends one, but nothing divides an existing item into two or ties the halves together; no candidate came within range.

c.spread_advantage().why: c.grants_advantage(when=) narrows a grant; nothing can ask what has_combat_advantage answered for another creature and re-publish it

c.spring_trap().found: components.Trap (ref, plus a 'gone off and not reset' field), query.can_act's trap branch ('could never make the attack they exist to make'), c.use_power(who=)
c.spring_trap().why: The model expects a trap to attack as itself and use_power acts on another entity's behalf, so firing one may already be sayable. Not run down: nothing in content or the loader ever constructs a `Trap`, so check whether a trap can be on the board at all -- the story engine that would field one is unbuilt.

c.stabilise().why: Nothing holds a dying creature short of healing it, so the death-save the card interrupts never happens. i3094p1 has already written the half that is writable (c.end_effect on the untyped burns) and named this as the rest.

c.stance(keep=).why: c.stance ends whatever stance was live by definition and at most one is ever held, so two at once has no spelling. Nothing else on Cast holds a second stance slot.

c.stand_costs(ActionType).why: c.grant_action only makes a thing cost less, and standing is priced in actions.legal with no modifier key

c.stealth_speed().why: skills.modifier totals ability, half level, modifiers and the armour penalty and has no speed term at all, and SkillCheck carries no movement, so there is no penalty to waive or soften. m3222a5 states it precisely and three unrelated files reach the same conclusion.

c.steer().why: MoveStart is a Decision carrying only actor and kind_ with no destination; refusal is the only lever, exactly as the row says

c.store_damage().why: i1028p1 needs two absent things: a bank on the item for damage dealt, which Magic does not carry (the same gap as c.charges), and a specific self-inflicted damage source to pay out on. Neither exists, and ctx['source'] cannot stand in for the second.

c.store_points().why: i1980p1/p2 want an *item* that holds power points; `c.points`/`c.spend_points`/`c.transfer_points` all read the creature's own pool and there is no second place to put any.

c.store_roll().why: No component banks a d20 result, and m6191a4 needs one substituted later for an arbitrary roll by an arbitrary creature. Same family as c.bank_reroll() and neither has a candidate.

c.store_row(ref).why: i3324x1 wants one item to remember another item's row. `c.link` joins two *squares* for movement, and `Item` carries ref, owner, uses and a spend callable with nowhere to hold a second item's ref.

c.stored_dose().why: apply_poison coats a weapon with a rider the calling row supplies, and a dose has no identity a second row can reach for. Nothing reads back what effects a creature is under or what type a burn is either, which is the other clause's hold.

c.stored_row().found: c.borrow_row is the pick-at-use-time workaround, not a store
c.stored_row().why: cf:wizard-arcanist-f0s4 says Powers holds known, prepared and expended and 'a stored row is a fourth state the tome owns'; i540p1 and i3320p1 want a row or an item ref held *by an object* and c.grant_row hands one to a creature. Nothing in components.py records either.

c.strip_resistance().why: Both edit Defences.resist directly and hand the entries back on the hold's on_end -- one type save-ends, and all of them for a duration -- so 'c.resist grants one and nothing takes one away' is false twice over, and p16586 can hang the strip on the escalate hook it already has.

c.substitute_check().why: c.reroll_check rerolls the same skill; standing a *different* skill's result in for a failed one has no expression. The distinction is the row's own and is correct -- a reroll and a substitution are different rules.

c.substitute_condition().why: c.immune refuses a condition outright and c.worsen adds one; nothing intercepts an incoming condition and swaps it for another. c.pre_empt substitutes a clause but only where the row laying it reads instead_of, which an arbitrary incoming condition does not.

c.suffering_save_ends().why: durations itself derives save_ends = when is When.SAVE_ENDS, so iterating effects.of(who) filters to them; i1341x1 and m5907a6 already iterate

c.summon(count=).why: m2331a2 says c.summon 'names nowhere for the vacated footprint to go', but the second positional argument *is* a square -- so 'each square it formerly occupied now contains one m2332' is a hand-written loop over query.squares(world, me) calling c.summon per square, which the global rule allows (it mints no rows).

c.summon_inline(decoy=).why: puts a targetable positioned double on the board without a stat block; unconfirmed whether a Conjuration is a legal target for the attack meant to dispel it

c.suppress(keyword=).why: the pair c.suspend_when is built on, reachable as c.world.effects; the keyword filter is a label-to-ref read, since labels lead with the laying row's ref

c.suppress_item().why: equipment.equip installs an item's rows from exactly that list, so a body can enumerate them, and c.forbid is 'cannot reach the row, and it comes back'

c.surface().found: c.terrain -- the fight, not the ground
c.surface().why: Grid carries light and difficult-terrain labels and nothing about what a square is made of, so there is no liquid surface for a movement mode to be granted over.

c.surge_bonus().why: query.surge_value reads mods.total('surge_value') and says a single bonus reaches every place a surge is cashed; the row already uses c.grants_in on the line above

c.surge_from(who).why: c.spend_surge(on=) spends one named creature's surge at one moment; nothing lends a pool as a standing permission

c.surges_of(ref).found: Health.surges / max_surges, c.surge_value(of=), c.spend_surge(on=), c.regain_surge(on=), c.no_surges(on=)
c.surges_of(ref).why: m1978a5 says 'nothing tracks another creature's surges or spends them from outside', and both halves are wrong: `surges`/`max_surges` are plain component fields and four verbs already take `of=`/`on=` for somebody else's pool. Reading the count is a door onto state that works.

c.surprise_round().why: three content helpers answer the question off live surprised holds. The row's real residual is that c.waive refuses cannot_act by design -- that wants its own symbol

c.surrender().why: REMOVED is cannot_act and cannot_move and p955 calls it out of the fight; unconfirmed whether a surrendered enemy should stay a legal target

c.suspend_effect().found: c.suspend_when, c.ignore_condition, durations.Effects.save (its context carries the effect, its label, conditions and ongoing types)
c.suspend_effect().why: Suspension exists for an effect you hold a handle on, and the save path knows exactly which effect is being rolled against. Not run down: whether SavingThrow.against identifies the effect well enough to find it again in world.effects.of(target) and hand it to suspend_when.

c.sustain(ref).why: Effects.sustain exists and actions._sustaining already drives it from the menu, including the two cases the default does not cover (sustaining early, choosing between two effects). What is missing is a Cast door and a way to find the effect, and c.dispel already finds holds by their label. p14124's 'has no verb' is literally true and 'has no mechanism' is not.

c.sustain_all().why: both are public; sustain-all is one loop over two existing methods content already reaches through c.world.effects

c.sustain_free().why: m4460a4 says 'a free one is not a cost the sustain machinery takes'; sustain_cost is typed `ActionType | None` and actions._sustaining only asks `encounter.can_spend(actor, eff.sustain_cost)`, which FREE satisfies. c.effect, c.aura and c.zone all already take sustain=.

c.sustain_grab().found: c.effect(sustain=) + c.on_sustain, c.grab(by=), c.conjure's returned eid
c.sustain_grab().why: c.effect takes a sustain cost and c.on_sustain is "what happens each time this effect is sustained", which is the announcement m6346a1 says nothing makes; and c.grab(by=) names a grabber other than the caster, which a conjuration's eid could be for i2393p1. I would check whether escape.attempt tolerates a non-creature grabber and whether a grab effect can be given a sustain cost.

c.sustain_row().why: f2842 says 'sustain= is a header field of the row that lays the hold', but the header only seeds a per-*effect* field: actions._sustaining offers the action for any effect whose sustain_cost is not None, and content rows pass it straight to effects.apply (warlock/level_5, bard/level_2). Setting it on the hold p377 laid is the clause.

c.swallow(dc=).why: escape.attempt returns False unless GRABBED_BY holds and _printed_dc finds its number through that relation; c.endable offers an action with no check

c.swap_initiative(a, b).why: the two-creature form already exists with that exact signature at turns.py:275; c.swap_initiative(other) is only the caster-pinned wrapper

c.telepathy().why: f3322 records that the racial trait carrying the range (`rt:r46-t2`) is declared `out_of_combat` and deliberately inert, so no creature carries a telepathy radius; f2470/f3317/f3395 each drop only the radius. No component field holds one.

c.teleport(adjacent_to=).why: to= names one square and the decider's offer is built from reachable squares; nothing filters that offer down to a set

c.teleport(no_sight=).why: c.teleport picks its destination through the decider and asks no sight question, so neither the permission nor the printed penalty for an occupied square can be written.

c.teleport(within=).why: c.grant_action's vocabulary has no teleport, so a standing teleport-as-a-move-action cannot be put in the menu, and c.teleport is an act taken now

c.teleport_as().why: c.shift_as is the same sentence for a shift and is implemented as a standing change actions.legal reads back; c.grant_action's docstring names the extension recipe for a new word. The teleport itself works. Nothing new is needed but the word and its reader, which is what shift_as already cost.

c.teleport_bonus().why: c.squares_for's docstring writes the worked example as `c.teleport(c.squares_for(c.ref, 8))` and c.extend_move's is "one more square on every swordmage teleport" - so "nothing lengthens a blink" is stale and the rows need only read their distance. The one genuine residue is a blanket bonus to *every* teleport, where extend_move wants a ref.

c.temp_hp(add=).why: resolve.temp_hp reads a temp_hp Mod off the receiver and adds it before the non-stacking comparison; the comment says it was put in for exactly this

c.temp_hp(remove=).why: resolve.temp_hp returns early for any amount at or below the standing pool, so no argument can lower it

c.terrain('natural world').why: c.terrain takes any free-form category, so the verb says this already; what is absent is data -- terrain.dress never writes a terrain word

c.terrain('outdoor').why: The reader exists; what is absent is data -- `terrain.dress` writes blocking squares, difficult squares and traps and never a terrain word, so `world.terrain` is always empty. By the `cf:fighter-weaponmaster-f3s0` precedent ('the gate is false today; it is asked anyway because it is the card's own sentence') f2718 is writable now.

c.terrain(at=).why: c.terrain is a property of the whole encounter -- the layer collision the brief warns about -- while c.scenery(kind, within=, of=) is how _near_a_tree asks the identical question

c.terrain(penalty=).why: c.terrain answers only whether the encounter is of that sort, and nothing applies an underwater weapon penalty anywhere

c.terrain(square=).why: Grid carries blocking, difficult, light, elevation, bridged and links per square and no material word

c.theme().found: c.feat(<the theme's level-0 row ref>, on=)
c.theme().why: c.feat is a plain is-this-ref-in-Powers.all; unconfirmed whether chargen ever assigns a theme -- nothing in chargen/ does, so the gate is sayable but always false

c.threatens(from_=).why: c.threatens writes reach and threatening_reach on the creature and movement._threat measures from its own square; nothing relocates a window to a conjuration

c.tome_powers().why: Upgraded from my own `probable`, deferring to slice 6. I marked it probable because I had not run it down; the agent did, and found `_tome_power` is live and reaches the dailies through `c.borrow_row`, walking the level ladder the card describes. A hand verdict outranks an agent's by default -- but not when the agent is the one who did the reading.

c.trade_accuracy().found: c.may (a per-use election), Weapon.thrown (no heavy/light split -- powers.warlord._heavy_thrown says no weapon in the model carries it)
c.trade_accuracy().why: Two holds and both are real: the weapon property is absent from the table, and c.may asks once when a trait arms where this card elects per attack, so there is no per-attack choice to offer.

c.trade_resistance().why: its docstring is 'the reaction that has no row' -- takes cost=/until= and charges the same immediate budget triggers._ask does

c.transfer(from_attack=).why: At the interrupt the effects the attack is about to lay do not exist yet, and c.transfer moves a live one -- a later question than the card asks. Nothing reads a pending effect list.

c.transform(into=).why: c.reanimate keeps the same entity's own numbers and c.form/c.mode change conditions and speeds, not the stat block. Nothing replaces a creature with a different one, which is m5787a0's whole printed effect.

c.transform_item().why: i2611p1 needs a magic item's base column swapped mid-fight, and the critical rider it names is applied by engine/equipment.py from that same column -- the Magic component records what the item may be laid on, not a live choice. Unlike a Weapon in Gear, nothing reads the base per use for a row to rewrite.

c.treat_as_enemy().why: Side.team is set at creation and no verb reassigns a live creature's side; c.dominate moves one attack, not the sides

c.treat_as_enemy_for_cover().why: Confirmed absent by the author with two greps, and independently: c.cover_in lays cover in a zone by side, and nothing reclassifies who blocks whose line per pair.

c.treats_allies_as_enemies().why: the opportunity gate filters watchers by query.enemies, which reads a Side no content row rewrites

c.trigger_trap().why: A trap's attack is a closure on `EnterSquare` keyed to its square, resolved through `resolve.attack` with the trap as attacker, so the attack path works and is reachable. Check whether a door can fire it without a creature actually entering -- the closure returns early unless `world.get(ev.actor, Health)` exists, so 'set it off from a distance' needs a victim or a refactor of `arm`.

c.triggering_attacker().why: The facility the symbol names exists, and its own docstring says the marker that stood on two rows 'wanted a method for a field the event has'. f619 still cannot be written, but for a different reason -- p3323 arms a watcher whose firing emits nothing -- so this marker needs re-aiming at that absence, not implementing.

c.two_handed().why: an empty off hand plus no shield is the grip; unconfirmed whether Gear distinguishes an unoccupied off hand from a one-weapon build that never had one

c.uncrit().why: f976's docstring states it outright: 'result.critical is writable and a critical can be *demoted*'. _next_blow_of_mine_crits proves the site -- the Hit interrupt window, writing both the event field and the live AttackResult, because the outcome is recomputed from that object. f3523's 'there is no moment at which a roll can put it back' is contradicted by a working helper in the tree.

c.underwater_penalty().why: c.terrain("aquatic") says where the fight is and nothing anywhere charges a penalty for it, so i3050x1 has nothing to waive. The gap is the rule, not the waiver.

c.undouse().found: the `doused` label convention in monsters.level_09.brutes._regenerates, plus c.end_effect
c.undouse().why: m1155a4 says there is 'no way to ask is this creature's regeneration switched off and no way to switch it back on from another creature's trait'. Asking is `any(eff.label == DOUSED for eff in world.effects.of(other))` and switching it on is c.end_effect, which exists for taking a live effect off early; content already imports these helpers across level files. The caveat is that each row chooses its own label, so the two blocks must share a constant.

c.unsave(succeed=).why: c.unsave turns a success into a failure; nothing anywhere writes saved = True, so there is no other half. Writing the cost alone would be a row that only hurts.

c.unseen_by(sense=).why: cast.py:8811 and :8833 grant blindsight and tremorsense as Mods keys with working ranges, query.sees_in answers for both, and c.has_sense asks after one on somebody else - so i2413x1's "tremorsense is not a sense the board has" and i1470p1's "blindsight is not a sense the board keeps" are both false. A row skips the hide per enemy with c.has_sense(..., on=foe).

c.untargetable().why: `c.cannot_attack(on=foe, against=me)` cancels at `AttackDeclared` so 'nothing is rolled and no rider fires' -- which is 'cannot be attacked' read from the attacker's side, and m5746a3 already uses the verb. m5848a2's and m5746a3's claim that 'nothing bars a creature from being a target' is wrong; the thin part is applying it per enemy.

c.untargetable(keyword=).why: nothing filters target legality by the attacker's power; the only cannot-be-targeted is Condition.REMOVED, which takes the creature off the board

c.use_power(origin=).why: The engine's only entry point for one row using another already takes an origin square, and c.use_power simply does not pass one through. A pass-through kwarg, which is the thinnest door in this slice.

c.uses_this_turn(ref=).why: Powers.times counts uses for the whole encounter and last_round holds a single round number, so neither can say 'twice this turn'. The row also names the second half -- the once-per-turn limit has to exist before anything can add to it -- and the distinctness clause on top.

c.using(ref).why: c.stance labels its hold label or self.ref, so lingers_label is 'is that row's state standing'; Movement.using is the collision. The remaining blocker is the brief giving no ref, which is defect=

c.vehicle_speed().why: the non-creature entities are Scenery, Conjuration and Trap, none of which carries a speed a passenger could read

c.vestige().why: The same read as c.active_vestige(): switching which of a set is live is a labelled hold that c.endable swaps and c.lingers_label reads, and c.build already records the leg. What is genuinely unrecorded is the set itself, which is the chargen sub-choice shape - I would check whether anything can hold a two-item pick per character.

c.vulnerable(by=).why: The kwarg already exists and its comment names this exact card shape: 'eleven rows print a scope -- "vulnerable 10 to the <monster>'s attacks", "vulnerable 3 to weapon attacks"'. The damage ctx carries 'source' and 'power', so 'vulnerable 3 to **your** elemental attacks' is a gate on those two. cf:sorcerer-elementalist-f2s0's 'c.vulnerable takes an amount and a damage type with nothing on the attacker's side' predates #471.

c.vulnerable(once=).why: DamageRolled is a Decision whose amount is mutable and read back by deal_damage, and c.watch(once=True) is the one-shot -- no vulnerability is involved

c.vulnerable(zone=).why: c.resist_in exists for the identical objection, gives on ZoneEntered, takes back on ZoneExited and clears when the zone ends

c.waive(when=).why: c.waive writes words into Conditions.waived with only an on_end undo and takes no predicate

c.wall(cost=).why: movement.costs is binary, 2 if rough else 1, and Grid.difficult's string is the sort of going rather than a price. Same gap p16653 names as c.zone(cost=)

c.wall_walk().why: i3016x1: 'the grid keeps a height and no surface to stand on sideways'. Grid has no vertical surfaces for a creature to occupy, and c.mode/c.phasing grant ways of crossing a square rather than a place to stand.

c.water().found: c.terrain -- the place, not the squares
c.water().why: All three rows need which squares are liquid, how many are contiguous and which are empty. Grid has no such feature and c.terrain answers only what sort of place the fight is in.

c.weapon_range().found: Cast.weapon_dice (the per-character replace(w) copy in Gear.weapons), Weapon.ranged / Weapon.thrown, resolve._long_range
c.weapon_range().why: RE-JUDGED with the cards. f1277 'increase its range to 10/20' and f2099 'its range increases to 20/40' are writes to Weapon.ranged on this character's own copy; both ALSO add a property, which is why each sits under two symbols. f1841 and f1843 want Weapon.thrown instead. c.weapon_dice performs exactly this write for Weapon.damage and needs no reader, because Gear.weapons holds replace(w) copies per character. The three symbols c.make_thrown(), c.weapon_range() and c.counts_as(property=) are ONE mechanism over 10 distinct rows -- f1841/f1843 carry two of them and f1277 carries two. #643.

c.widen_area().why: Both levers exist -- `widen_areas` lays a `blast_size` modifier for close blasts and bursts, `resize_aura` changes a live aura's radius and announces it -- but `cf:ardent-f0` is deliberately 'a snapshot, not an aura' and hardcodes `c.within(5)`, so neither reaches it. Check whether that row can be made to read its own `CloseBurst(5)` header plus `blast_size`; the facility is one layer from f3321.

c.within(extend=).why: the distance is a literal 3 inside the row's body and no modifier reaches a literal; c.bonus('range') moves the printed range line instead

c.worsen_save().found: c.reroll_save(keep="worst") (triggered rows only), Cast._rolls_twice_higher and the damage_twice_lower key as the shape
c.worsen_save().why: durations.Effects.save rolls once and consults no 'twice' key, though it builds a rich context for gates, so a standing roll-twice-keep-lower across every save against one attack's effects has nowhere to live. The damage path has the analogue and the save path has none.

c.zone(blocks_sight_except=).why: Zone.exempt's own docstring names this row: three rows want an exemption by sense, a set cannot say that, and those rows keep their markers

c.zone(cost=).why: difficult terrain is worth exactly one extra square in movement.walk and difficult= takes a label, not a number

c.zone(difficult_exempt=).why: Zones.difficult_squares answers per square with no notion of who is moving, unlike the sight-blocking reader exempt= feeds

c.zone(ends_on=).why: the walk-into pop is reachable as m5602a3 despawns its conjuration; the other half needs the conjuration to have defences, this row's other marker, so it cannot go green alone

c.zone(side=).found: Zone.owner exists and no terrain property reads it
c.zone(side=).why: Read the component: Zone carries owner, but Zones.difficult_squares returns a plain square-to-kind dict and blocks_sight is documented as 'binary and symmetric: it blinds both sides, which is terrain'. obscured is directional through the looker's senses, not by team. So nothing keys a terrain property on a side, and the field a side would hang off is unread.

c.zone(sight_limit=).why: literally 'no line of sight to any creature more than N squares away', read by query.unseen_by, hung on the zone through _while_inside

c.zone_exempt().why: documented as creatures this zone's sight-blocking does not apply to, read by query._blinding_squares; the rider mutates the live zone as m2507a3 mutates Zone.difficult

cf:barbarian-f1s0.why: The ref is printed on cards and no row in the tree carries it - features/primal_shadow.py:19 says so directly and docs/blocked.json asks for it, and items/waist.py:384 is a third row waiting on the same absence. This is a content declaration gap, not an engine one.

cf:monk-f0c0.found: the five refs appear only as a list in content/items/implement_b.py
cf:monk-f0c0.why: No `@power` declares cf:monk-f0c0..c4 anywhere in content/features, so c.use_power and c.borrow_row have nothing to point at. The gap is content -- declare the five per-tradition rows -- and nothing stands in for them.

cf:monk-f0c1.found: nothing -- cf:monk-f0 is declared, cf:monk-f0c1 is not
cf:monk-f0c1.why: Checked the registry: cf:monk-f0 is in REGISTRY and cf:monk-f0c1 is not, so the five per-tradition attack rows really are undeclared. c.flurry_of_blows() has already landed and i724x1 records that it was not the hold; this is content that has not been written, not a facility.

cf:monk-f0c2.why: The five flurry cards are declared - FLURRIES = ("p7448", "p11207", "p13123", "p16131", "p16132") - and c.flurry_of_blows() derives from the registry which one the monk holds, "so a row can watch it, spend it, or hand back a use". f3701 does exactly that watch today; implement_b.py:114's "none of the five is declared" comment is stale.

cf:monk-f0c3.why: i1197p1 says cf:monk-f0 hands out one attack row per monastic tradition and 'none of the five is declared', so c.use_power(..., again=True) has nothing to point at. The symbol is an undeclared ref, not a missing facility -- it is content to write, and nothing in the tree stands in for it.

cf:monk-f0c4.found: nothing -- the five refs are named in a todo tuple and declared nowhere
cf:monk-f0c4.why: grep finds cf:monk-f0c0..c4 only inside items/implement_b.py's FLURRY tuple; no @power declares any of them. This is content work (write the per-tradition attack rows), not an engine gap -- c.use_power(again=True) is already the payout the rows want.

cf:sorcerer-f0s1.why: f2175's body writes both halves; its docstring called the keyword half the standing gap while the last line of the body wrote it. APPLIED

cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.found: nothing -- but no engine work either
cf:sorcerer-soul-nat20.why: cf:sorcerer-f0s2 lists this rider among its own dropped clauses and i2693x1 says 'the natural-20 rider this card loosens to a 16 is that row's own dropped clause, so there is nothing standing for a wider trigger to fire'. The ref is simply undeclared; the natural roll is on the attack event, so this is a content row to write rather than a facility to build.

cf:warlock-f1c0.found: nothing -- cf:warlock-f1s0 names it and no row declares it
